articleTitle: Computer Aided Load And Voltage Data Analysis For Use In Power System Planning
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Using an integrated computerised load and voltage data base can enhance reliability and quality of power system. Data Collection, analysis and reporting becomes easy. Changing computer technology makes it easier to implement. In this paper an easy and complete computer aided load and voltage data analysis procedure for use in power system planning is discussed.

publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Channel modeling and perforumance estimation of block codes with periodic and changeable interfeaving degree in the digital mobile channel
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, a simple partitioned Markov model with three states for the digital mobile channel is presented based on a field test curve. The expression of the model and its transition probability matrix P are obtained and error distribution probability P(n,m) is calculated In terms of the matrix P, From P(nm), the performance for a few of Interleaved block podes, which are BCH codes and Golay code is estimated by use of the BSC model and the simulation results is given. At the meantime, additional time-delay caused by the periodic interleaving is obtained. A few of group of the changeable Interleaving degree scheme is presented and the comparison between the periodic and changeable Interleaving degree scheme is obtained by means of the analysis to the error characterization in the digital mobile channel.

articleTitle: The Estimating On Performance To Interleaved BCH Codes Applied To The Mobile Communication Channel
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, the Markov model with three sates is used for the probability model to the mobile communication channel with long burst error. The error distribution probability P(n,m) for the mobile channel is calculated in terms of the relation between the parameters of the model and the error statistical parameters of the model and the error statistical parameters, and from this, the performance of error-correcting interleaved BCH codes are estimated, which can be applied to the mobile communication channel. As the first time, the method is proposed that the performance of interleaved BCH codes applied to the mobile channel is estimated by use of the parameters of BSC channel and the simulation of te performance of a few interleaved BCH codes is made in comparison with the result of the estimation.

articleTitle: 2-D Edge Feature Extraction To Subpixel Accuracy Using The Generalized Energy Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Precision edgefeature extraction is a very important step in vision. Researchers mainly use step edges to model an edge at subpixel level. In this paper we describe a new technique for two dimensional edge feature extraction to subpixel accuracy using a general edge model. Using six basic edge types to model edges, the edge parameters at subpixel level are extracted byfitting a model to the image signal using least-squared errorfitting technique.

articleTitle: Application Of Artificial Neural Networks To Load Flow Solutions
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are gaining popularity in many engineering and scientific applications due to their high computational rates, ability to handle nonlinear functions and a great degree of robustness. Load flow studies are important to arrive at power system planning, control and operating strategies. Sometimes, utilities are unable to perform certain functions, involving several load flow solutions in real time mode e.g. power system optimization and security analysis due to availability of slow and unreliable conventional load flow methods. This paper reports the development of fast load flow method based on neural network which can be used for such real time applications. A feed forward model of the neural network based on back propagation algorithm has been used for the load flow probelms and the method has been tested for two sample ac systems. The proposed model has been found to provide sufficiently accurate results.

articleTitle: A Smooth Variable Structure Position Control Of Dc Motor
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Variable structure control using sliding mode technique has been widely used for different electrical motors in position loop. Its advantages are insensitivity to parametric variations and ability to reject disturbances like sudden load applied to the motor shaft. However, for a low inertia systems it exibibits more chattering. In this paper, a sliding mode controller for a very low inertia system (Printed circuit motor) is proposed. A new chattering reduction technique is also proposed here. Controller structure is a hybrid one where analog circuit has been reduced to a minimum level. Computer simulation as well as experimented results are presented to verify the chattering reduction technique.

articleTitle: Spectrum efficiency of a mobile cellular radio system using direct sequence spread spectrum
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum Multiple Access (DS/SSMA) is proposed for mobile cellular systems with coherent phase shift keying (CPSK) modulation. Spectrum efficiency and bit error probability are evaluated taking co-channel interference into account for uncorrelated (fast) Rayleigh fading and (slow) log-normal shadowed signals, The analysis is significant for a mobile radio system using Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum because in such a system co-channel interference is always present.

articleTitle: A 0(1) Time Deadlock Detection Scheme in a Single Unit and Single Request Multiprocessor System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new deadlock detection scheme, which is more efficient than existing ones. We assume a special case system where each type of resource has one unit and each request is Iimitecl to one unit request at a time. Unike the previous deadlock detection schemes, our new method takes 0(1) time for detecting deadlock, and O(n+m) time for handling reeource reIease, where n end m are number of processes and resources in the system, respectively. The deadlock detection latency is thus minimized end is constant regardless of m and n. Release handling tskes longer than conventional detection schemes. However, in a multiprocessor system environment, operating system can handle the release on the fly running on a seperate processor, thus not interfering with user process execution. To some class of applications, a predictable and zero-latency deadlock detection scheme could be very useful.

articleTitle: Automatic Color Difference Discrimination System With Capability Of The Dark Eyes' Color Perception
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes the development of the automatic color difference discrimination system using CCD color Imager. The CCD color Imager used for the system of the present work Is provided with the capability of the same color difference discrimination as In the dark eye. This new automatic color difference discrimination system can be used to the production line.

articleTitle: Study And Analysis Of High Capacity Survivability Performance
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Formation Of Loop Impedance Matrix --- A New Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper reports a novel approach for the formation of loop impedance matrix for power system fault studies. Network loops are selected in such a way that further changes in the network can be represented very easily with minor modifications of the loop impedance matrix. The approach finds its justification in solving problems like relay coordination where multiple number of fault studies are required.

articleTitle: Passive And Active Harmonic Filters For Industrial Power Systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper will initially provide a brief review of the various conventional passive harmonic filters that are used in many industrial power systems. This paper will then discuss the fundamental principles of some recently proposed filters, often referred to as active filters. Two particular types of active filters, one based on analog signal and the other on Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) control, have been recently implemented by the authors. Results from laboratory investigations will be presented. Potentials for the use of these filters in other areas of power systems will also be described. Finally, advantages and disadvantages of these filters will be discussed.

articleTitle: Cost effective feasible clustering for hierarchical topological design of large computer communication network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Hierarchical clustering technique is used to minimize the cost for the topological design of a very large systern,compu ter communication network [1]. In this paper we present a technique to achieve integer solution of the problem such that a real net work may directly be constructed. Though the solution does not ensure global-optimization, it provides a good practical results.

articleTitle: Transaction Management in a Database Driven Real Time System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Real time systems are characterised by the existence of such transactions, that need to complete execution within limited time. Because of their special nature, these transactions cause scheduling difficulties. Traditional concurrency control methods are unsatisfactory for their management. In this Study we propose a method to handle real time transactions efficiently. We propose a solution by adopting transaction classification and a mixed concurrency control to provide an efficient technique for management of real time transactions. Extension to the case of a multitude of real time transactions has also been considered.

articleTitle: An algorithm for discrete event logic simulation on distributed systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Increase in the complexity of VLSI digital circuit design demands faster logic simulation techniques than those currently available. One of the ways of speeding up existing logic Simulation Agorithms is by exploiting the inherent parallelism of the sequential version. In this paper, we explore the possibility of mapping an event driven logic simulation algorithm onto a cluster of processors interconnected by an ethernet. The set of events at any simulation time. step is partitionecl by the Master Task (running on the host processor) anlong the Worker Tasks(running of the other processor's). The partitioning scheme ensures a balanced load. Each Worker Task determines the fanout, elementts, evaluates them independently and comes up with the new event list which is passed onto the Master Task. After receiving the event lists from all the workers, the Master Task increments the simulation time step, computes the new event list partition for the next simulation cycle. We have implemented this distributed logic simulation algorithm on a set of 8 VAXstations using CT - a package for distributed programming. The paper concludes with a note on the speedup figures obtained on the ISCAS benchmark circuits.

articleTitle: Frequency tuning of bipolar ring oscillators
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Bipolar ring oscillators are used extensively in digital gates for the measurement of gate delays. As an application to analog circuits, bipolar ring oscillators may be used as a voltage coutrolled oscillators (VCO) if the frequency tuning of the oscillator is performed by voltage/current. In this paper three different techniques of frequency tuning of ring oscillators are described. A PLL circuit is designed and tested using bipolar ring oscillator.

articleTitle: Radial Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Radial voltage stability poses problems for power system planners and operators. This paper presents methods and aids which can meet the quite distinct needs of both planners and operators, with an emphasis on the practical aspects of the problem. An actual disturbance is described in which the first phase was due to system voltage instability, and subsequent events are due to radial voltage instability effects. The instructions available to the operators were not adequate for the situations they faced. Without using the approach described in the paper, it took them an hour and continuing difficulties before they could reach an acceptable operating state.

articleTitle: From Model Based Specifications to Functional Prototypes
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Signature Identification using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Traditionally, the human signature has been used for the identification of a person. With the modernization of optical technology, it is now possible to electronically process human signatures and use neural network techniques to validate these signatures. The signature may involve visible parameters such as size, orientation, peaks and valleys. It may also involve invisible parameters such as depth, pressure variations, vibrations and consistency. This type of information can be suitably used for the training of feedforward neural networks for the purpose of signature identification. This article will present an approach to extract some of this information and demonstrate how this information can be used to verify signatures.

articleTitle: A Tool for Real-Time Performance Monitoring of Parallel and Distributed Systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents the concepts, architecture, and features of a tool for instrumenting parallel and distributed systems. This capability will be useful in evaluating alternative architectures and strategies for distributing application software, detecting performance bottlenecks, quantifying and fine-tuning real-time performance, detecting and isolating behavior anomalies, and characterizing the behavior of specific algorithms under desired stimulation conditions. The Honeywell instrumentation system provides a flexible capability for selecting and customizing existing instrumentation functions, synthesizing new instrumentation functions, and tailoring/scaling instrumentation to a particular architecture or application domain.

articleTitle: Dynamic State Estimation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A Dynamic state estimator is proposed to give better representation for the time evolution of the state of the system. The Dynamic state estimation utilizes, in addition to the static one, the previous estimate of the state, along with the information on its reliability and the changes that the state is likely to have undergone. This approach consists of predicting the state vector based on past estimation, followed by a filtering process performed when a new set of measurements is available. Dynamic estimator for a Power system is proposed based on exponential smoothing and least squares estimation techniques. For computational purposes a decoupling principle is applied, where active and reactive variables are decoupled. This decoupling principle reduces storage requirements and computational time.

articleTitle: Speech Enhancement Based On MMSE-STSA Estimation And Residual Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Three types of noisy speech enhancement algorithms based on Minimum Mean-Square Error Short-Time Spectral Amplitude estimation (MMSE-STSA) are experimentally compared, especially under low SNR. Among them, MMSE-STSA and MMSE-LOG-STSA have been reported [1],[2] and MMSE Short-Time Relative Spectral Amplitude (MMSE-REL-STSA) estimation is derived in this paper. The modified gain function and center clipping are proposed to reduce 'residual noise'. It is shown that these algorithms can improve the speech SNR of 5- -10dB by 3.4- 12dB, and provide enhanced speech with colorless noise.

articleTitle: Robust State Feedback Control for Structured Uncertain System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Multiobjective Hydro Thermal Scheduling
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In the present paper, hydro thermal scheduling has been proposed as a multiobjective problem. Minimum cost and minimum emission under the constraints of water availability have been chosen as two goals which are clearly non-commensurable objectives. A simplified direct method has been proposed, If there is a power limit on any generator(s) tile modifications necessary to take into account same has been outlined.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Augmented Baseline Multistage Interconnection Network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a class of fault-tolerant multistage interconnection networks (MINs) named as Augmented Baseline Networks (ABNs ). A technique is described for making MINs more reliable and cost effective. The Proposed technique results in reduced number of stages in a network. Performance and reliability study show that ABNs achieve a significant improvement over unique path MINs and compare favorably with other multiple path MINs.

articleTitle: Improvements in load flow studies using strengthening of fast decoupled models
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper presents a 'Strenghtened Fast Decoupled Model (SFDM)' and a novel approach for the adjusted load flow analysis withoud any need for (complete or partial) refractorization of second constant-slope matrix relating the reactive mismatches and voltage correction variables. The novel approach presented for adjusted load flow solutions is found to be very effective in resolving many of the problems associated with adjusted load flow studies using Fast Decoupled models without any additional computational burden. Results obtained using standard IEEE test systems are presented. Test results establish that the proposed approach for adjusted studies is quite stable and can also be used effectively with XB and BX models. Based on the nature of the elements of the two constant-slope matrices of SFDM, a single matrix model (SMM) which uses only one constant-slope matrix for solution of active and reactive power mismatch equation for correction variables /spl Delta//spl delta/ and /spl Delta/V is also presented. It eliminates the storage, formation and triangularization of second-constant slope matrix, which is essential in case of conventional Fast Decoupled model. Test results on IEEE systems establish that SMM takes lesser CPU time and memory than XB or BX models even for normal systems.

articleTitle: The Manufacturization of the Software Quality Improvement Process
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A comprehensive model is proposed to pattern the software manufacturing process after the hardware manufacturing process, in spite of fundamental differences between the two processes. The failure data produced in each process phase is analyzed and used to control the movement to the next phase. At each phase, the failure rats can be compared to the quality criteria, and a decision can be made whether to proceed to the next phase or repair the software. If the quality criteria are not met, in-process root cause analysis can be performed to improve the product.

articleTitle: Introducing Shared Memory in Hypercube Architectures using Multistage interconnection Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We propose a cache-based hypercube system with multistage interconnection network connected to a shared memory. We present analytical models for such systems in which a single copy of shared data is maintained. Markov models are developed to find out the hit ratios of caches for various data movement policies. We also obtain the average penalty of these policies in terms of average distance between the hypercubes and the referenced shared data to find out the best policy which can minimize this penalty.

articleTitle: Capacity of a slotted code division multiple access system for wireless in-house network communications
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The capacity of indoor (in-house) packet radio channels is investigated for a star-connected multiple access network with a unique spread-spectrum code for each user considering direct sequence spread spectrum (DS/SSMA) communication. Such a protocol is commonly known as a code division multiple access (CDMA) method. The influence of micro diversity on the channel capacity is also studied, assuming a Gaussian approximation for Rayleigh fading interferers. The capacity of a radio channel is defined as the maximum throughput obtained for varying offered traffic to the channel. Computational results are presented for both slow and fast Rayleigh fading indoor radio channels with BPSK (binary phase shift keying) and DPSK (differential phase shift keying) modulation schemes.

articleTitle: Adaptive technique for the minimization of EOG artefacts from EEG signals using TDL structure and nonlinear, estimation model
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: BEG records are often contaminated with extracerebral signals called artefacts and one of the main disturbances is due to eye movements which generate an electrical activity called EOG. In this paper, we use an adaptive noise cancellation scheme in a novel way for the minimization of the EOG artefacts from corrupted EEG signals. This method is based on the fact that the transfer function of the biological neuron can be modelled as a sigmoidal nonlinearity. Comparison of the time plots as also the smoothed linear prediction spectra show that the proposed method effectively minimizes the EOG artefacts from corrupted EEG signals.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of interference rejection techniques in spread spectrum communication
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Inherent processing gain of spread spectrum communication provides relatively higher degree of interference resistance. Two techniques have been discussed providing interference immune communication, while operating in heavy interference enviroments. First is digital whitening, accomplished by the use of transversal filter whose coefficients are found either using Levinson's algorithm or algorithm developed by Burg. Second technique discussed, provides very impressive theoretical performance against CW interference in DS-SS system. An estimate of interference level is used to suppress interference prior to correlation process in the receiver. Then a multi-tone interference rejection in FH-SS system is proposed, error signal during every hopping interval is appropriately used to adjust the timing clock of VCO synchronizing the output of digital frequency synthesizer to the incoming signals. At the end performance of all these techniques are analyzed.

articleTitle: The Role of Public and Private Sectors in the Evolution of Telecommunications Networks - The Japanese Experience and Some International Comparisons
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Pollution Performance Of Metal Oxide Surge arresters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Distributed alternate local routing in dynamic networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A concept of Iocally alternate paths, as opposed to node disjoint and link disjoint paths, is introduced in the context of networks with frequently changing topology. The paper dicusses the generation and utilisation of such paths. A route selection strategy is presented which avoids looping of packets resulting from moving over longer alternate paths. The flexibilify of alternate path routing, in conjunction with local topology information, also helps in reducing route updation overheads. An algorithm for providing the required topology information is also presented.

articleTitle: Range Sensor-Based Environment Model Acquistion for Autonomous Robot
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an environment model acquisition technique for robot navigation in an unknown terrain, which requires no prior information about the environment, and which can handle concave Curved/polygonal obstacles as well as convex ones . In this method, features extracted from the coefficients of X/sup 2/ terms which approximate sets of 4 consecutive range sensor data with second-order polynomials by the Least-squares method. Then a "local environment map" representing the robot's line of sight environment can be built. This map is helpful for a local planner to devise safe paths in an unknown environment.

articleTitle: Predictive control of blast furnaces
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Personal communications - new challenges for digital services
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Engineering tricks in minim12ation of combinational logic for c/sup 3/ system design
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper presents some interesting ideas in Combinational circuit minimization. There are many different existing techniques for such minimization such as K- mapping, tabular technique and extended tabular technique etc. There are several limitations In these techniques eg. failure to handle functions of variable number of inputs, failure to handle functions of different variable even when the number of variables for functions is same etc. The paper is to report some algorithms using which these limitations of the existing techniques may be overcome. The paper also reports a new technique known as break up alqorithm which will be very helpful in such minimization. All the new algorithms process the given truth table to generate new truth table for minimization.

articleTitle: Application of the Homotopy MLthod to Finding Economic Dispatch Solutions
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The functions of the cost curve and transmission losses are existing nonlinear, simultaneous subject to equality and inequality constraints. Mathematically, the solutions of the nonlinear equations of economic dispatch problems may result in multiple solutions, singal solution or no solution. Conventional methods may fail to find all the multiple solutions if the initial guess values are not appropriately located within the convergency region. To overcome this difficulty the homotopy method is suggested for the solution technique. In this paper the homotopy theorem is incorporated with the B-coefficient method to solve the economic dispatch problem. Not only the initial value is easily obtained but also all the multiple solutions can be obtained. So the exact least cost of economic dispatch can be derived.

articleTitle: Using Untampered Metrics to Decide When to Stop Testing Software
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Exhaustive testing of large software systems is prohibitively expensive and practically impossible. However, most software development process managers erroneously assume completeness of the test programs. This has often resulted in an incorrect system evaluation and the release of poor quality products to the field. The understanding of this limitation can become a strength by driving the testers to optimize the positioning of the test programs (robust testing). The observation that software errors tend to form clusters (design holes) permits the use of statistical failure analysis to pinpoint the largest and most likely defective areas. It is essential to periodically halt testing and analyze the test failure data in order to optimize the use of the remaining testing resources and interval. The entire test program can be stopped when the likelihood of residual design errors is small enough.

articleTitle: The PC as a General Purpose Real-Time Computational Tool
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Shape Invariants Of Reflectional Symmetry From Elliptic Fourier Descriptors Under Parallel Projection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The determination of reflectional symmetric planar shapes is important for pattern recognition, shape analysis and quantitative shape recovery. In this paper, forms of shape invariants for reflectional symmetry using elli]?tic Fourier descriptors are derived. They are found Ito be independent of shape rotation, translation and orl:hographic parallel projection. By theoretical analysis, these invariants provide sufficient information for (i) detection of reflectional symmetry and skewed symmetry, (ii) the axes of symmetry and skewed-symmetry, and the skewed-transverse axis, (iii) the root locus of the gradient vector (p,q) that can interpret the vkewed symmetry as a real symmetry.

articleTitle: Static task allocation for heterogeneous distributed computing systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of static task allocation of concurrent programs for heterogeneous distributed computing systems, i.e, given a set of n concurrent communicating processes and a two processor distributed computing system, in which each processor may have certain resources not available with the other processor (i.e., unique resources), to which processor should each module be assigned so as to maximize the throughput? Our problem is a variant of the task allocation problem considered by Stone/sup 2/ in that we consider concurrent execution of the processes comprising the task. Also we explicitly consider the resource usage costs for each module thereby resulting in a more realistic model of the distributed system. This task allocation problem is NP-hard and hence, we provide an efficient heuristic algorithm for obtaining satisfactory suboptimal solution to it in a reasonable amount of computation time. Our algorithm works by constructing an augmented task graph and taking a load balanced mincut on it and has a time complexity of O((n+m)/sup 2/) where m is the total number of unique resources in the two processor system.

articleTitle: Voice Mail Based on IBM PC
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The voice signals are digitised and stored on the hard disk of a IBM compatible PC. Each message is stored and retrieved as a separate file on the disk. Since each message is addressed as a file, users can be served with total security. The system is used on a EPABX. The system has been designed using the chip MC 3417. The hardwaree and software details of the system developed and its working is presented.

articleTitle: Multi-priority implementaion of the ring/bus protocol - a more efficient version of the token ring approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The IEEE 802.5 Token Ring system has become a standard media access protocol (MAP) for interconnecting the nodes in a medium-speed Local Area Network (LAN). This essentially operates using a circulating token where a node captures the token in order to transmit it's packet; it then forwards the token to the next downstream node, The system provides priority operation with up to eight levels of priorities. This protocol requires a processing delay of one or more bits at each node thereby increasing the Ring Latency Time (RLT). This paper proposes a new Ring/Bus protocol to reduce this RLT for better performance. This is done by replacing the nodal delay of the Token Ring by a switching arrangement at each node, The proposed Ring/Bus system can also support multi-priority service. Analytical results on the performance of this new proposed scheme is presented along with some simulation results.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control Of An Interconnected Power System Using Integral Control
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper an integral controller is present for load frequency control of an interconnected power system. The integral controller is a classical controller [3] used for load frequency control to satisfy the hyperstability condition for taking care of the parameter changes of the system. The controller possesses an attractive merit of being easy to implement and a load shedding scheme can be incorporated for case studies. The simulation results show that good control performance can be obtained by the integral controller.

articleTitle: A novel decision-directed receiver for detection of GPM signals
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A novel Decision-Directed Receiver (DDR) has been arrived at based' on heuristic considerations for coherent demodulation of arbitrary Continuous Phase-Modulated (OPM) constructions received over AWGN channel. The complexity of the DDR is a linear function of the observed symbol intervals. However, repeated processing of the received (signal + noise) waveform segments is required. The error probability analysis of the DDR for a subclass of CPM known as CPFSK is presented. It is noted that the low-complexity DDRs are attractive by virtue of their superior error performance relative to the well known Average Matched Filter (AMF) receivers, at least for certain modulation indices, for example h = O.S.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Vision System For Automated Inspection Of Surface Mount PCBS
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents the techniques used to inspect for defects on Surface Mount PCBs. Focusses were made on five different types of defects, namely, miss ing components, misalignment, wrong orientation of I.C. chips, wrong parts and poor solder joints. Thus five separate algorithms had been developed to detect these faults. The technique of windowing was employed to reduce the amount of redundant data to be processed. Preprocessing functions like convolution as well as all image processing tasks are performed on the window regions only, saving tremendously on computation time. Experimental results showed that these algorithms are reliable; fast and cost-effective.

articleTitle: A New Concept For Thyristor Phase Controlled Var Compensator
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper describes a new concept of thyristor controlled shunt VAr compensator. Present method utilises a natural commutated converter scheme for VAr control operation. The effect of dc offset voltage control on VAr drawn by the converter has been investigated. Investigation of fundamental and harmonic frequency characteristics of the source current is presented here.

articleTitle: A congestion control scheme for interconnected local area networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We investigate congestion control issues in an interconnected network where several local area networks (LANs) are connected to a high speed backbone network. In such a network, traffic congestion may occurs due to the difference of transmission speed and/or workload be tween the high speed backbone and the lower speed LANs. To release the congestion and achieve high throughput, we propose a congestion control scheme and evaluate the performance of the scheme via simulation. In our scheme, each bridge always informs the number of available spaces in its buffer to the other bridges. It gives the highest priority in transmission to the packets of which destination bridge has the largest available buffer spaces. Moreover the scheme restricts the maximum number of the packets which have the same destination in order to prevent that the packets destined to the congested bridge stay in the buffer for a long time due to low transmission priority and shut out the other packets destined to the uncongested bridges. Simulation results show that the scheme significantly reduces the packet loss and provides high throughput in the backbone network.

articleTitle: Power Electroics: Present and Future
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Microprocessor Based Thermal Model Approach For Protection And Optimum Utilisation of Power Thyristors Transformers And Drives
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The application of micro-processors has greatly facilitated the advanced simulation and modelling techniques. The modelling approach not only helps in estimating the certain parameters in a device or a process but also provides the means of protection either directly or as a backup to the physical transducers. Therefore the need of modelling techniques becomes significant. This is especially true where is not physically possible to install the physical transducers. In the paper, the real time modelling approach are described for power thyristors, transformers and drives. It is being emphasised that microprocessor based modelling could effectively be used for protection and optimum utilisation of these devices. The paper explains the significance of thermal parameters and their use ia mathematical equations in order to compute the various temperaturs in real time application. Based upon the thermal history, corrective action could be taken prior to plant shut-down. The thyristors have complex thermal network & also some of the thermal time constants are very low. This necessitates the very fast real-time computations. A typical microprocessor based system and associated peripherals is being described in the paper. In the case of the transformers the method suggested could be used for computing the winding hot spot temperature in real-time under fluctuating load conditions.This inturn is used to calculate the used Iife of the transformer on day to day basis. Taking into the consideration the actual ambient temp. conditions, the approach could be useful In overall energy management with number of transformers in operation without excessively stressing any individual one.Thus ensuring protection as well as optimum utilisation.The paper considers oil immersed transformers only. A simplified approach for DC motors has been explained which could be used as a backup protection and also a prior warning before the temp. reaches alarming limits.

articleTitle: Speech Recognition using Back-Propagation Neural Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Back-propagation neural networks are used for speaker-dependent speech recognition of isolated words. The speech is digitized and its features are extracted by using Fast Fourier Transforms. Then Linear Frequency Cepstrum coefficients were calculated. The entire system of speech recognition using a back-propagation neural network was successfully implemented on a personal computer (80x86 microprocessor based) for words "one" through "five" with an overall accuracy rate of 89%.

articleTitle: Formal Representation of Semantic Data Models in Type Theory
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A programmable cellular automata structure for built-in self-test
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The regular structure of 1-D and 2-D cellular automata as a Built-in Self-Test (BIST) structure have been proposed [Hort'89, Hort'90, Das'89, Das90b, DRC91b]. In the present paper, the performance of 2-D CA as a pseudo-randorn pattern generator has been evaluated. The potential increase in the local neigh bourhood structure for 2-D CA has led to better randomness of the generated patterns as compared to LFSR and 1-D CA. The quality of the random patterns generated with 2-D CA based BIST structure has been evaluated by comparing the fault cover age on several benchmark circuits. The design of a Programmable Cellular Automata chip has been proposed as a versatile BIST structure.

articleTitle: Computerized control of sizing machine in textile industry
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper discusses an actual implementation of control of sizing machine of a textile industry (TECOM, Nanded) by using the IBM PC/XT [1,9]. The parameters to be controlled are the level of size mixture in the size mixture in the size box, temperature of the size mixture in the size box, and moisture contents in the warp which is controlled by controlling the temperatures of the drying cylinders. This paper discusses the computerised control of sizing plant in textile industry in which there are normally 4 to 8 sizing machines.

articleTitle: Singly and Doubly Fed Capacitor Self Excited Generator and Microprocessor Based Voltage Regulator
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Linear Suboptimal PWM Switching for Microprocessor Controlled Inverters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new PWM technique for microprocessor implementation of single phase inverter is proposed, This stratagy is an approximation to the optimal characteristics. It is a trade off between memory space, response time and total harmonic current distortion (THD). Optimal switching angle variations are approximated by defining a linear modulating parameter making the calculations (on-line computation) simpler together with no quantization errors. The strategy is developed for single phase 2 level PWM and then extended to 3 level PWM. Comparisions are made of the results thus obtained with those given by other PWM techniques reported earlier.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Load forecasting on short term basis is formulated in the framework of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. The maltilayered perception model using back propagation algorithm makes possible to train the ANN with training patterns. The training patterns (past data) can act as input in various ways which are explored and reported here. The trained network is tested on the MSEB data, and the results are discussed. The network can be trained in a dynamic way by using the most recent data.

articleTitle: A novel scheme for designing error correcting codes using cellular automata
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel scheme of designing a new class of Error-Correcting Codes (ECC) using a simple structure built around additive cellular automata (CA) [1,2,3]. The regularity and cascadability of the three neighbourhood CA structure makes it an ideal choice for VLSI implementation. A scheme for the construction of Single-Error-Correcting (SEC) and Double- Error Detecting (DED) ccde is proposed which can be easily extended for information bits of any arbitrary length. Further, the basic scheme can be modified to generate code with arbitrary distance t. When compared to existing schemes, the method can be found to be much more. efficient in respect of silicon area overhead.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of a Local Gain Scheduling Power System Stabilizer for Inter-Connected System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new 'Gain Scheduling Stabilizer' for interconnected power systems has been described in this paper. The design of the PSS is based on a priori information about readily available machine and excitation system parameters and 'Observation' for a certain duration of time of the network from the bus of the machine concerned to ascertain the electrodynamic coupling of the machine to rest of the network. The computational complexity of this PSS requires the use of relatively sophisticated computing system. Though, such computers are now available, they are not in common actual power plants. With this in view, the PSS design has been modified so that the adaptive gains are selected in real time based on the operating conditions and worst case network parameters. The modified PSS can be implemented using on-line computers having capabilities similar to those of ordinary PCs or even /spl mu/P systems with moderate memory and computational capabilities.

articleTitle: Capacitive Energy Storage: An Aid for Dumping Frequency and Tie-Line Power Oscillations
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Fast acting energy storage devices can effectively damp out electromechanical oscillations in a power system, because they provide storage capacity in addition to kinetic energy of the generator rotor, which can share the sudden changes in power requirement. A new scheme using a small rating Capacitive Energy Storage unit for the improvement of the dynamic performance of a power system is proposed in this paper. A comprehensive digital computer model of the two-area interconnected power system including the governor deadband non-linearity, steam reheat constraints, boiler dynamics and the generation rate constraint is developed for the analysis.

articleTitle: LAN protocols for high-performance distributed and concurrent computing
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The number and variety of evolving high-performance distributed and concurrent applications motivate the development of novel and more suitable protocols for their support. We have developed a protocol framework within which concurrent applications may be developed and executed in a straightforward manner on heterogeneous LANs/ The protocols are specifically oriented towards the needs of concurrent applications, and are designed to be robust, efficient and lightweight. The protocols offer reliable and fast packet delivery in a variety of modes, including point to point broadcast, and dynamically variable multicast semantics. In addition, they support several high-level concurrent computing funcuons in an integral mamner, including global extrema and other arithmetic operations, polling, distributed consensus, and synchronization mechanisms. We discuss the salient design aspects of these protocols, describe the syntax and semantics of the user- interface protocol primitives, and, present performance results for varying network sizes and types.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Techniques in Queueing Approximations for Delay Time in Computer Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The estimation of delay or response time is of vital importance in computer communications networks. Queueing theory offers considerable solutions, via exact analysis, or approximations. However the inherent limitations of statistical methods limit the scope of queueing analysis, especially when networks are complex and under dynamic operations. This paper discusses the possibility of fuzzy variables used in queueing systems.

articleTitle: Comprhensive UHS Distance Protection Via Knowledgh-based Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A knowledge-baaed decision system developed for SHV transmission line Protection. This Paper describes the two major aspects of the system, (1) Knowledge reprenentation, (2) logic process, for decission fault distance calculation. Different knowledge representation techniques are discussed with their relative performances. The developed system is shown to be reliable and stable under different fault condition, Including zero fault inception angle. Computing burden is quite reasonable and ultra high speed (UHS) performance can be achieved with commercial microprocessors.

articleTitle: Design Of A 8085 Microprocessor Controller For A Three Phase Converter With Fourth Leg
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The three phase converter discussed in the paper is a conventional three phase converter with a fourth leg. This operates both in rectifier mode and in inverter mode. By properly triggering the thyristors the negative portion of the output voltage is eliminated in the rectifier mode and the positive portion is eliminated in the inverter mode. This method of control improves the input power factor. This paper gives detailed procedure for generating the firing pulses for the thyristors using 8085 microprocessor to operate the converter both in the rectifier mode and in the inverter mode. A software is developed and tested. The output waveforms are obtained both for rectifier and inverter modes.

articleTitle: An Expert System For Decision Making In Nonmonotonic Domain
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We propose in this paper a new technique of decision making in nonmonotonic domain to tackle databases having uncertain, imprecise, incomplete and inconsistent information. The technique uses a network called Fuzzy Petri Net (FPN) in order to represent a set of propositions and the logical connectivity among them. We have successfully applied the technique to develop an expert system (ES) for criminal investigation.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model for Performance Evaluation of Multiple Access Schemes for a Stat Configured Data Communication Computer Network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes the simulation model for performance evaluation of time-slotted multiple access protocols, applicable to a star data network. The simulation model is of synchronous discrete event Monte-Carlo type and consists of six major functional modules. The features of these modules are discussed in the paper. The approach towards developing the model has also been included. The results of the performance of our proposed multiaccess protocol are also given in the paper.

articleTitle: Comparative Simulation of High Speed Unidirectional Local Area Bus Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: With a rapidly growing trend of using fiber-optics as transmission media, there is an immense interest in high speed local area networks (LAN s). These networks offer an efficient and cost-effective means of communication within a relatively small geographical area. Bus and ring topologies are the two most popular topologies for fiber optics LANs. In this paper, however, we will only consider bus topology. In a typical fiber optics bus network, transmission is unidirectional. In our study the time is slotted and each station attempts to transmit in an empty slot persistently with a preassigned probability. Messages are assumed to be of variable length and are segmented into fixed size packets such that each packet fits in a slot. Fair access to the shared transmission medium can be achieved if access probabilities are assigned propetly to all stations. Three probability assignment schemes are considered: uniform, linearly increasing, exponentially increasing, and optimaI. The average delay per message for this network is studied through a simulation program for various probability assignment techniques. This study shows that there is significant difference in performance of these techniques.

articleTitle: New Reduction Technique For Distribution Feeders
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Prototyping of Medical Image Analysis Algorithms in a Functional Language
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes a prototyping environment for image analysis, constructed by the marriage of low-level, `C' coded image processing routines and the functional programming language Miranda. This combination provides a secure and purely functional programming environment, whilst maintaining reasonable efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of a Reconfigurable, Application-Specific LAN with Enhanced Scope
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The International Standard Organization (ISO), in an effort to encourage "Open" networks, developed the Open Systen Interconnect(OSI) reference model. The OSI model describes the functions of each layer in broad terms, not specific implementation. Standard available LAN specifications describe the type of cable, speed, frame format, media access methods etc. as general industrial standards but in many of the real time applications, there may be specific communication requirements which may not be satisfied by using off-the-shelf LAN subsystem. Attempt has been made to identify the speciality of the Application-specific networks in this paper. General design methodologies of the application specification Network are discussed particularly in view of distributed real time systems. A set of hardware/software modules have been developed for this purpose. These design methodologies have been tested and varified while implementing a specific real-time application at SHAR centre, Sriharikota for their communication requirement.

articleTitle: A digital frequency relay for over'under frequency detection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Grounding system design for an undergroung hydro-electric plant - a case study
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Conflict Resolution Strategy In Expert System With Ambiguous Knowledge Base
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper provides an exhaustive overview of the conflict resolution strategies used in the existing rule-based expert systems and proposes new strategies based on heuristic functional approach for the expert systems of future generations. The proposed technique is superior to the rule existing ones since it improves stability in the line of reasoning of expert for such systems. Illustrations have been chosen from an expert system for Trigonometric theorem proving.

articleTitle: Remote DOS disk server on a unix machine
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A Remote DOS Disk Server runmng under UNIX has been designed and implemented. The service is provided by a daemon process running on the UNIX machine. The server software is built using the socket interface for network communications provided by BSD systems. In this server, each user has a login name and is authenticated by a password during login. The server can support multiple simultaneous login sessions. To access a remote disk, a user must map a remote drive number to that disk. A user may map to any dosdisk on the server provide he has the required access rights. The owner of a disk may grant access rights of different types both to individual users or to user groups. Protection is provided by having an Access Control List (ACL) for each dosdisk.

articleTitle: Personal communications network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Wireless access and egress gives the service providers an added flexibility for personal comm unications which deals with linking people rather than their telephones. Currently, personal communication needs are partially satisfied by several wireless services including cellular mobiles, pagers, satellite and cordless telephones. Based on emerging concepts, architectures and standards, enhancements to existing wireless services and several new services are now under consideration; the new services include digital cellular systems, and wireless PBX and CENTREX services. Globally, each of these services can be based on different standards and have unique characteristics. This may prevent the ubiquitous offering of a 'truly' global wireless services, Personal communications network (PCN) is seen as a vehicle to offer global services. This paper discusses the PCN concept, architecture and evolution.

articleTitle: Delay Performance Evaluation of a Token Ring LAN Under Real-Time Load Conditions
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, the delay performance of the Token Ring LAN which supports real-time traffic along With conventional non real-time traffic has been evaluated. Real-time traffic is characterised as that which requires packets to be delivered within a prespecified delay upperbound. Real-time packets delivered after its deadline are considered lost . Network parameters such as the number of nodes supporting real-time traffic, size of real-time and non real-time packets, and the percentage of real-time packets in the network have been varied to demonstrate their effect on the mean delay. A discrete-event simulator using SIMULA has been developed on ND-530 Computer System. IEEE 802.5 standard protocol has been implemented. The results can be used for planning of networks with real-time traffic by determining whether the real-time data transfer requirements of a particular application can be met by the network.

articleTitle: Multivariable Invariant Systems Design Via the Inverse Model Principle
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Developmetn of an optimum flight control system
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Simulation of nuclear reactor dynamics for control system design & testing
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The simulation of nuclear reactor dynamics for the purpose of testing the reactor control system hardware and software in a closed loop fashion requires a real time simulation of the reactor neutronics and associated processes on an inexpensive computer. The later is found achievable if only the distinct range of manouvres in neutron power, its rate etc. during controlled operations of the plant is well recognized and suitable model modifications are made enabling faster solution without compromising on accuracy within the domain of interest. Studies with such model modifications as well as enhancements in the efficiency of numerical solution through the use of implicit techniques are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: OPS Systems And Reason Maintenance: The Nexus
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: OPS5, one of the widely used production system languages, offers many interesting facilities like structured representation of facts of a domain, nonmonotonic deduction etc. However, it suffers from some major drawbacks such as its inability to reason with revocable actions and handle dead ends and domain constraint violations. In this article, we present a new OPS architecture (called OPS91) which uses the RMS methodology to maintain reasons for actions performed, as a partial solution to the above problems. We show that the new architecture can solve a wider class of problems and hence, is a better production system model for problem solving. The OPS91 architecture is implemented in common LISP on a MicroVaxII work-static n and is currently being tested.

articleTitle: Satellite Based Data Networks for Developing Countries
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Developing countries usually lease satellite transponders from neighbauring countries/International bodies or at the most have a single satellite in the orbit due to high cost of the satellites. In such countries, satellite resources must be used efficiently. Data network examples have been discussed in this paper with Indian Satellite communication context. Authors have suggested most suitable and technically viable satellite based common data networke, using existing Satellite Earth station infrastructure, which conserve satellite and national resources. The paper describes present configuration of satellite based individual corporate data networks, its limitationes, optimum configurations (baaed CDMA/SSMA, AA/TDMA and SPADE technologies), Indian scenario, availability of the satellite equipment and future trends.

articleTitle: Moment Invariant Features used as Inputs to a NeuraI Network to Recognise Numerals
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm in which the moment invariant features of a numerical character are presented as inputs to a neural network. The image is digitised, by a frame grabber card plugged into the extension slot of an IBM AT computer. Three moment invariant features derived from the geometrical moments were extracted and fed to the neural network. The neural network, used back propagation learning in its training, classifies these features and attempts to produce the desired output. Noisefree and noisy images of various variances of the ten numerals were experimented and the results are reported.

articleTitle: Modelling Analysis And Improvement Of Transient Performance Of Field Controlled D.C. Shunt Motor Drive Using Phase Locked Loop Technique
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper deals with the application of phase locked loop control principle to the speed control of D.C. shunt motor employing field current variation. The modelling and stability analysis of the above scheme is carried out for small as well as large variations of the motor load. The transient performance of the drive is greatly improved when an additional stabilising signal derived from the derivative of the output is applied. The analytical results obtained for a typical. 230 V 7.5 H.P., 1000 RPM D.C. Shunt motor are presented. This scheme has the advantages of low cost, compactness and ease of control over the armature voltage control method.
