publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Automated Analysis of Transmission for Transportation Facilities and its Synthesis Through Dialouge
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: New Concept for Co-ordinated Power Plant Control
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A Pedagogical Tool For Learning Lisp
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: LISP is one of the most used languages in the area of AI applications. For a student os AI the knowledge of LISP is an advantage. This paper reports the design of an intermediate language for a subset of LISP. It makes use of the concept of Canonic Interpretive form (CIF) to develop a Directly Executed Language (DEL) instruction set for programming language LISP. The DEL system also serves to be a good environment for learning the architecture of a High Level Language (HLL). On account of its compactness and elegance, LISP is a good paradigm for studies on DEL concepts. LISP DEL has been implemented on system HP-1000/40. The sysem has substantiated that the DEL is efficient both in terms of storage space and execution time requirements.

articleTitle: Simulation Of Optical Heterodyne Single Filter FSK System With Laser Having Non-uniform FM Characteristic
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The simulation results for an optical heterodyne single-filter FSK system using DFB laser having nonuniform fm characteristic are presented. Two line coding plans, vizo alternate-mark-inversion (AMI) and delay modulation (DM), are considered for the laser driving signal to overcome the adverse effect due to laser nonuniform fm response.

articleTitle: The Global Positioning System The Technology of the 90s
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The NAVSTAR Global Positioning System (GPS) provides extremely accurate three-dimensional position and velocity information to users anywhere in the world. This paper attempts to present a comprehensive view of this new technology and its utilization with a focus on the user segment of the system. It describes the basic concept, signal structure, system characteristics, accuracies, error sources, antenna requirements, support software, and controls. The varied and modern applications of the system, with emphasis on its differential and dynamic mode of operation, is also presented. Finally, research and development work, ongoing at Wilkes University, towards an operational GPS workstation, will be presented.

articleTitle: Computer-aided Design Of Matched Converter-motor Pair For Induction Drives Based On Effective Harmonic Utilization
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Present trends in the design of asynchronous drive systems is to use standard induction machines in conjunction with solid-state converters with minimized time-harmonics in their supply profile, The paper proposes an alternative approach wherein the seeming ill-effects of time-harmonics may be used with advantage in improving the torque developed in the drive systems. This approach, named the 'Dual Convergence Approach', leads to the design of matched converter motor pair, with specially designed motors capable of using select time-harmonics in supply and is readily amenable to computerizationp both for design and selection of the system. Designs based on proposed methodology have been extensively tested with encouraging results.

articleTitle: Off Design Exergy Audit Of A Captive Power Plant Of Kribhco Fertiliser Unit
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Exergy analyses of the captive power plant of KRIBHCO, Surat. Gujarat State carried out. The analyses include the study during the normal operation and the operation with the outage of one of the HP heaters. The outage of one of the HP heaters gave exergy losses under the off design operating conditions. Grassman diagrams are presented and discussed, The information regarding the exergy losses in process and power plant steam headers and the let down valves indicates the need of an optimal layout of the units in the plant.

articleTitle: On-line Simulation of Robot Manipulators
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The amputation of the Forward Dynamics problem plays a major role in the real-time modelling and simulation of robot manipulators, The efficient and computationally inexpensive solution of this problem will boost the design of red-time robot simulators. This work proposes to solve this problem by employing a pardel processing approach. A heuristic load-balancing procedure is used to distribute the dynamic equations of a robot am over a network of parallel-processors. The network is connected in a multiple instruction multiple-data stream (MM)) formation. The efficiency of the algorithm is demonstrated by a case study.

articleTitle: New Loss Formulae For Real And Reactive Power Optimization
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Two general loss formulations have been proposed in this paper for total system real power loss and series reactive power loss and series reactive power loss. These are expressed as quadratic functions of both real power and pv-bus voltages. Quadratic expression for series reactive power loss has also been proposed only in terms of reactive power control variables, i.e., pv-bus voltages, shunt reactive power compensation and OLTC. Moreover, closed form expressions have been derived for these coefficients as well as A-loss coefficients, utilising sensitivity coefficients and partial derivatives of real and active power losses with respect to optimization variables. Hence, updating of loss coefficients is quite efficient. Because of closed form expressions, solution of linear set of equations is eIiminated.

articleTitle: Fluctuating Load And Steam Demand Management For Minimum Cost
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Electrical Models For Real Time Operator Training Simulators
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Simulators are very useful in various activities like design, analysis, optimization, and training. Depending on the scope and extent of simulation, the hardware and software complexity vary. Electrical models developed for detailed power system studies are proven and well established. In order to use them in the real time operator training simulators, precise approximations are needed. In this paper modelling of electrical elements and the actual implementation scheme for the operator training simulator are discussed.

articleTitle: Optimisation Of Avalanche Photodioide For Optical Detection For Wide-band Demodulation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: To realise high-quality optical transmission systems Avalanche Photo- Diodes (APD) are required to have superior sensitivities as optical detectors : with high quantum efficiencies, high speed of response and low multiplication noise. In this work, an optical fiber link has been designed and tested, with an APD and a transimpedance amplifier at the receiver. The receiver sensitivity of this moderate bandwidth optical fiber communication link is investigated and optimised as a function of an APD operating point. The experimental results have been compared with the simulation results. The avalanche gain (M) of an APD is sensitive to the reverse bias voltage and temperature. As the bias voltage varies, M and F(M) vary non-linearly as a function of temperature as defined by the Miller and Mc Intyre equations. Since the excess noise factor F(M) increases with M, there always exists an optimum value of M that maximizes the Signal-to-Noise ratio. With regard to maximum Signal-to-Noise ratio at an optical receiver output, a figure of merit for a given APD Is proposed to optimise the excess noise factor F(M) for given optical detection process as a function of multiplication factor M at various spot frequencies in the wide-band demodulation system.

articleTitle: Complexity Reduction of Robot Dynamic Equations
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Simplification and approximation procedures have been developed for the complexity reduction of robot dynamic equations. A symbolic manipulation approach has been followed in order to produce the simplified and the approximated model expressions in a form directly compatible with numerical computation programs for robot simulation and control problems. The procedures have been tested making reference to a PUMA robot.

articleTitle: Trends in Power Station Control Room Design
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Dynamic state estimation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A Tool For Learning Foreign Languages
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The Reading Assistant is a multimedia interactive system designed to help people learn a foreign language. It does so by promoting learning in context: language material is always presented as part of originally unedited foreign-language text. Students learn a language by reading text with the aid of tools such as online dictionaries, grammars, and translation aids. The recorded pronunciation of individual words And sentences is also available and can be played back as often as needed. The Reading Assistant allows all aspects of the interaction to be controlled by the student, and minimizes information overload through the use of statistical grammars. While the system is designed to help English speakers loam a second language, the results of an experiment show that it could easily be extended to teach English as a second language to non-native English speakers.

articleTitle: Slot-switched Self-routing In A Non-crossbar Optical Switching Architecture
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A novel duration switching method for self-routing in multi-stage non-crossbar (optical switching architectures using a two- wavelength header scheme is proposed. Closed form expressions are derived for the worst-case signal-to-crosstalk ratio and the insertion loss and the maximum size of the architecture is estimated from these.

articleTitle: Neural Network Approach to the Enhancement of EEG Signals in the Presence of EOG Artefacts
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Human electroencephalogram (EEG) contains useful diagnostic information on a variety of neurological disorders. However, like all biomedical signals, EEG is also contaminated with many unwanted signals or artefacts which seriously affects its clinical usefulness. One of the main disturbances is due to the eye movements, which generate an electrical activity called electrooculogram (EOG). In this paper, we propose a Neural Network (NN) approach to the enhancement of EEG signals in the presence of EOG artefacts. We recast the EEG enhancement problem into the optimization framework by developing an appropriate cost function. The cost function is nothing but the energy in the enhanced EEG signal which is obtained through a non-linear prediction formulation, unlike the conventionally used linear prediction formulation. The minimization property of the Hopfield Neural Network is exploited to solve this problem. The optimum non-linear predictor coefficients obtained from this minimization algorithm are used to estimate the EOG artefact which is then subtracted from the corrupted EEG signal, sample by sample, to get the artefact minimized signal. Thus the power and efficacy of the NN approach have been exploited for the purpose of enhancement of EEG signals in the presence of EOG artefacts.

articleTitle: Energy Conservation And Distributed Capacitive Compensation Using Capacitive Ballasts for Fluorescent Lamp Circuits
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Inductive ballasts for fluorescent lamps are lossy. High frequency electronic ballasts albeit excellent performance are too expensive to be adopted in developing countries. L-C ballasts have some fine features. A suitable starting circuit is designed. Such capacitive ballasts offer energy conservation, leading power factor operation, low voltage start up. Besides the distributed capacitive compensation is highly beneficial to the utilities.

articleTitle: A VLSI implementable versatile electronic neuron and its applications
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A VLSI implementable design of an electronic neuron is proposed. The most important feature of this neuron design is its versatility for use in many applications. The synapse strengths in this neuron have provision for real time programming and hence the neural network built can be truly adaptive. In this paper the application of this neuron for feature extraction and character recognition have been described.

articleTitle: A Parser Generator for Unification Grammar Formalism with Gap-Handling Facility/spl dagger/
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Unification grammar formalisms are very useful in the syntactic analysis and the semantic interpretation of natural language statements. However, we must use special techniques (e.g. gapthreading) to capture the long-distance dependencies, which are very common in natural languages. It makes the grammam less clear. This paper introduces island constraints into PATR-like formalisms to handle gapping in the natural language sentences automatically. An incremental compiler is proposed to translate the grammar rules, and generate the optimized codes. The basic code-optimization principle is restriction unification first and inheritance unification last. It not only preserves the operation semantics of the original grammar rules, but also improves the performance of the generated parser. For the designs of semantic interpreters and machine translation systems, the grammar formalism is further extended to represent semantic rules and transfer rules. This paper also shows that a tandem-processing model can be obtained by a slight change to the original generator.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Expert System For Voltage-var Scheduling
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: An offline rule based expert system is developed to assist in controlling voltage-VAr/reactive power in a modified IEEE 14 bus power system. Inference strategy adopted for expert system is based on fuzzy logic. The system non linearity and coupling effect is simulated forming a sensitivity tree. Use of fuzzy logic and fuzzy sets in modelling interconnected complex modern power system for accurate control of voltage profile and thereby for management and control of reactive power is shown here.

articleTitle: A Critical Appreciation On Fuzzy Logic Controller Design
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, without denying the merits and novelty of the technique of approximate reasoning we propose an alternative method for inexact reasoning. It has been established that the proposed technique gives at least the same, if not better in all cases, results as found from the application of Zadeh's compositional rule of Inference.

articleTitle: On Line Identofication of a Delay Process
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, one of the recently reported recursive identification procedures has been applied to a practical system so as to identify its parameters. The dead time of the system is identified by candidate structure method reported recently by using the HP- Vactra PC with input and output subsystems, the results which have been found satisfactory, are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Validation in Distributed Representations
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In the Hoptield model of content addressable memory, the number of spurious attractors is exponential in the dimensionality of the memory. Hence it is highly likely that the system converges to a spurious memory on an arbitrary input. It is desirable that the system has a way cf checking whether its state corresponds to any one of the stored patterns. In this paper we show that it is possible to validate the patterns in a distributed fashion. The model uses compIex activations and synapses for this purpose. The genuine memories are defined to be real attractors. Under some assumptions we show that the expected number of spurious attractors is negligibly small. We also calculate the capacity of the model.

articleTitle: Analysis of an unsymmetrically fired phase controlled rectifier used as a static var generation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new scheme of Staic VAR Generation employing a Three Phase Full Controlled Asymmetrically Fired Line commutated rectifier with a single inductor as load is proposed. The technique controls the system lagging ractive power without drawing any active power from the line. The scheme uses only one inductor and hence economical than Thyristor Switched Reactor (TCR) scheme.

articleTitle: Microcomputer based instrument control system using GPIB
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This article presents an inexpensive way of design and implementation of microcomputer based instrument control system using GPIB (General Purpose Interface Bus IEEE 488 standard). The GPIB interface card has been implemented with the Intel three chip set: 8291, 8292, 8293. This GPIB interface card is connected to the backplane of 8086 based microcomputer system, to control and to communicate withthe three GPIB compatible instruments: FLUKE (5 1/2 digit DMM), KIKUSUI (60 MHZ) Oscilloscope and IWATSU (SM-2701) FFT Analyser. The required software driver package has been developed using 8086 assembly language programming. This controller can program any compatible instruments through GPIB to perform various tests, set the parameters as applicable to the instruments. Using this controller various projects related to microprocessor based instrumentation can be implemented. This controller can also be a part of an Automated Test System (ATS).

articleTitle: Maximum likelihood sequence estimation and its VLSI implementation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In the reception of Generalized Tamed Frequency Modulation (GTFM) signals corrupted by noise, Maximum Likelihood Sequence Estimation (MLSE) technique has been successfully used to minimize the bit error rate. In this paper, we review the MLSE in the context of GTFM, and report its imple-menation in VLSI 2 micron CMOS technology. Testability issues in the IC design are discussed.

articleTitle: State assignment of finite state machines for optimal implementation using MUXs
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A multiplexer (MUX) in a versatile powerful building block for logic synthesis. This paper describes a method for the synthesis of control part of a VLSI system using MUX. Here, the states are encoded such that such next state function is realized by an optimal/near optimal tree network of 2-to-MUXs.

articleTitle: Power system modelling and simulation for design of 2*90/-40 Mvar SVC
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The performance of static-VAR compensation plants (SVC), which are widely in use in electrical power systems, need to be checked with detailed studies in order to design optimal compensation schemes with respect to amount of reactive power, location of installation, control strategy, distortion of system voltages (harmonics). A two-step design flow is described, which leads to an optimized final design of all components. The parameters for representation of the equipment are of significant importance for the design of the SVC and are explained together with planning principles and criteria to be adopted to the different studies. The approach was tested during the design of a 2*90/-40 War SVC.

articleTitle: Software Validation of a Digital Switching System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A Digital Frequency Relay For Over/under Frequency Detection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Under frequency relays are used to shed automatically certain portion of load whenever the system frequently falls to such a low level as to threaten the stability of the power system. In this paper a very simple digital frequency relay is proposed for this purpose. The main component of this relay is a simple digital frequency measurement circuit which gives better accuracy than present day available frequency delays. This relay can also be used for over frequency detection.

articleTitle: Segmentation Of Range Images Using Morphological Operators
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper we present an algorithm for segmentation of range images using the digitisable operations of morphology. The range image is segmented into planar primitives based on their orientations. The concept of Neighborhood Plane Sets (NPS) introduced by Mukherjee et al [10] has been used. The NPS proposed in [ 10] has been augmented by considering four more orientations. A straightforward technique for the extraction of NPS has been proposed. NPS extraction is followed by a smoothing step. The final segments are extracted using a particle marking scheme.

articleTitle: A Homotopy Method For Stabilization Of Multivariable Systems With Structural Constraints On State Feedback
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Various structural constraints on the state feedback gain matrix, K, used in the control of a multivariable dynamical system arise because of the way feedback is realized. Static output feedback, decentralized state feedback, simultaneously stabilizing state feedb, ack for several operating points of a, system, and two-controller feedback are some examples of control structure realizations which impose constraints on K. We cast each of the problems in a general class of problems of stabilizaLion of multivariable systems with such structural constraints into a problem of solving a system of equalities and inequalities which is then solved using a continuous realization of the gradient projection method and a barrier method under the homotopy framework. Our method is illustrated with two examples.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for Reliable Information Transmission
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Error correcting codes are widely used for improvement of reliability of information transmission and storage in all digital communcation applications. The new trends in communication systems require some new techniques which can improve the performance and enhance the speed to handle massive amounts of data. The artificial neural networks have shown the potential to meet these challenges.

articleTitle: Object Recognition Based On Indexing In 2D Environment
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Model-based object recognition has attracted considerable attention in the vision paper presents a model-based two dimensional object recognition system using feature indexing under a linear transformation through geometric hashing. The objects are represented by their dominant invariant features under a linear transformation in the normalised orthogonal coordinate frame. The goal of this paper is to solve the 2D recognition in'the industrial environment in an efficient way and reduce the net computational overhead. The proposed algorithm is also able to identify a partially occluded object in cluttered environment. The paper shows how the symmetry of the object can be exploited to reduce the model data storage and to speed up the matching process. The matching is done through its feature set tuples. The feature set includes both the local and global features of the objects, which helps to recognise the object more accurately.

articleTitle: Development Of An Expert System Shell For Use In Monitoring Of Industrial Plants
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper the details of the Intelligent Diagnostic & Decision Support System (IDDSS), a hybrid tool for developing Expert Systems(ES), are presented. While the shell can be used for developing expert systems in any domain features required for expert systems in the area of monitoring have been specially incorporated. The shell is developed using the 4GL of the ACCELL development environment and the knowledgebase is created within the UNIFY database. As the shelI has been developed for monitoring it has facilities for data collection directly from the DDCS. Though the shell is developed under the UNIX operating system it can access and use any DOS software. The discussion is presented in four sections. In section I a brief introduction the kind of problems encountered in industrial pIants is provided. This is followed by the discussion on the development of the shelI in section II. In section III an exampIe from process control problem and some of the features of a rotating machinery fault diagnosis system under development are presented. In section IV which is the concluding section , the limitations of the system and the possibility of extending the scope of IDDSS is discussed.

articleTitle: Comprehensive UHS Distance Protection Via Knowledge-based Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A knowledge-based decision system is developed for EHV transmission line distance protection. This paper describes the two major aspects of the system, (1) Knowledge representation, (2) logic process, for fault distance calculation. Different knowledge representation techniques are discussed with their relative performances, The developed system is shown to be reliable and stable under different fault condition, including zero fault inception angle. Computing burden is quite reasonable and ultra high speed (UHS) performance can be easily achieved with commercial microprocessors. The need and significance of UHS relaying for EHV transmission lines are by now well known. It improves power system reliability, transient stability and reduces the damagre caused to the equipments. There are caused to the equipments. There are apparently two distinct approaches in distance protection taken to achieve high speed performance. One is based on fast estimation of power frequency components using Kalman filters symmetrical. components etc, The other approach relier on the information content in the high frequency part of the fault induced components. The later is popularly called as traveling wave (TW) based distance rela ying. Both the schemes have their own advantage and dioadvantages. The initial position of the fault induced voltage and currents are heavily dominated by travelling waves. So for the initial period of a few milliseconds, signal to noise ratio is higher for TW-based relaying and lower for power frequency based relaying. However, for near zero-fault inception angles the magnitudes of the travelling waves are very low and it is very difficult to detect these faults using TW-baoed distance relaying. The problem can be solved by combining both the methods with greater computing burden and algorithm complexity. A novel approach is presented here to solve this problem using knowledge-based system. The beauty of this system is that the whole spectrum of the information -ontalned In the fault Induced signals (limited by the sampling frequency) is considered in a very simple manner. The idea of the knowledge-based system came from the fact that post fault voltage and current waveforms are dependent on fault distance. The authors, for a time, were engaged in applying different signal processing techniques to develop TW-based distance relaying. It is observed that fault distance can be estimated from the fault-induced signals using various signal processing techniques e.g. correlations of the signals, power spectrum of the signals signal cepstrum . The decission process related to all the algorithms are more or less same : detecting some strongest component and its position. The information in the other part of the power spectra on correlation functions cannot be easily treated or related to fault distance always, thus motivating the application of knowledge-based system. The informations in fault induced signals are stored as a function of fault distance with the help of digital simulation. The information may be the raw post fault signals or some pre- processed versions of it. However, fault-generated waveforms are also dependent on various system parameters, other than fault distance. Some of the system parameter variations are taken account of in the knowledge representation part. Even then the searching procedure will be too much time consuming and some amount of higher level knowledge has to be applied to cut down the searching procedure. This technique helped the proposed relay achieving UHS performance with commercial microprocessors.

articleTitle: Load Testing Strategy for a Distributed Voice/Data Platform
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Measuring performance of a voice/data platform consisting of hardware and system level software is a difficult task without the use of a specific application package. In this paper, the load testing strategy for a voice/data platform and the performance results for both inbound and outbound calls are presented. The hardware platform consisted of an AT&T Definity Generic 2 Private Automatic Branch Exchange (PABX), two multi-processor AT&T 3B4000 computers connected over a Local Area Network (StarLAN), dual ISDN links between System 85 PABX and 3B4000 computers. System level software consisted of UNIX System V Release 3, communication software for handling ISDN Q.931 messages and Adjunct Switch Application Interface (ASAf) messages. ASAI is an AT&T protocol between PABXS and applications running on adjunct processors. For both inbound and outbound calls, a high degree of voice/data synchronization can be achieved through ASAI level messages over ISDN links between AT&T Definity Generic 2 PABX and any application running on an adjunct processor (e.g. AT&T 3B family computers).

articleTitle: Pollution Performance Of Metal Oxide Surge Arresters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A metal oxide surge arrester (MOSA) under the effect of conductive pollutants presents two problems namely the insulation performance of the porcelain housing which is more or less similar to insulators working under polluteted condition. Modelling of this type of problem has drawn considerable attention of the researchers and resultq have been published in literature [1,2,3]. But the second problem as sparkover performance of the active parts consisting of coupling and grading capacitances and MO varistors is less known. Taking the consideration of coupling and grading capacitances and non-linear resistance and capacitance of element equivalent circuit becomes very complex. In literature [4] Shibuya et al. has analysed the MOSA behaviour under pollution by taking equivalent circuit diagram considering only coupling capacitance not grading capacitances. And they have not reported temperature effect. There report is limited to variation of voltage distribution with dry band length. In this paper with the help of computer program the results of the investigation on how contamination may affect internal circuitry of MOSA has been reported. Analysis has been also done for watt loss and its thermal effect on MOSA.

articleTitle: Edge Detection In Range Images With Multiple Window Operators
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid approach towards the detection of edges in range images. It tends to combine region growing and one dimensional orthogonal polynomial fitting techniques for the detection of edges in range images. Edges detected by such method possess good localisation property. The incorporation of region growing process eliminates internal micro edges and pzoduces a segmentation map. The edge and segmentation maps when conveyed to the higher level recognition process, may prove valuable for object identification purposes.

articleTitle: The Frequency Instability In Large Power Systems : An Emergency State Analysis
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper reviews the effects of frequency variation on the performance of power system under the power reserve and no power reserve conditions. The system degradation during the frequency instability is studied when the system has no power reserve through analysis and graphical representation. The emergency control measures to curb the frequency instability and to protect the system are discussed and proposed. A case studv of the frequency instability experienced in Indian power system is presented here to support the importance of frequency instability study.

articleTitle: Model Based Recognition Of 2-D Occluded Objects
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A model based method for the recognition of 2-D occluded objects is presented. Initially, to reduce the number of models to be considered for identification from the model database, signatures comprising 5-tuple curvatures are used. Next, point to point matching known as exact matching is used to find the correct models present in the scene. The results are illustrated for an occluded scene consisting of industrial objects.

articleTitle: Partitioning and Scheduling for a Parallelizing compiler
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We have addressed two important issues in parallelizing compilers, partitioning ( of DOALL loops, which is a subpart of the original partitioning problem) and scheduling of task graph. Partitioning of DOALL loops becomes important because of the finite number of processors available in the system, overheads associated with executing any process on a processor and the granularity of the process. We propose a method to find the number of iterations to be assigned to a processor which does not require the number of processors available be known beforehand. We also propose a dynamic scheduling algorithm for task graph using the primitives provided by the MACH operating system. The algorithm works for UMA architectures. Issues in NUMA architectures are discussed briefly at the end.

articleTitle: Separation Of Images Of Overlapped Objects
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A simple algorithm has been proposed to separate the images of overlapped objects from binary Image. Algorithm is designed using Mathematical Morphological operations and, hence, can be Implemented on parallel machines.

articleTitle: Protocols for fault-tolerant systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We report, the design and implementation of a fault-tolerant message switching network. Failures andfailure masking are examined under the framework of Open Systems Interconnection model of distributed systems. Failures are masked by hierarchically structured entities or by replicating entities in a group, The paper describes peer communication protocols assuming the peer entity to be a group consisting of sub-entities. These peer protocols resulted in simplified group communication protocols needed to synchronize and manage the group.

articleTitle: Pragmatic TCM codes in linear & band-limited non-linear satellite channel
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A lot of work has been done to search for convolutional codes that can give the best maximEd free distance which is the criteria indicating the goodness of the codes' performance level used with Viterbi decoding. For high-rate convolutional codes, simplicity of the Viterbi decoder was sorted for ease of application, resulting in the development of punctured codes [11, which are obtained by periodically deleting a part of the bits of low-rate convolutional code. This not only enable a simplistic encoder / decoder structure, but also enable rate-selectable convolutional encoder / decoder to be implemented. In line with the search for simplistic encoder/ decoder structures, Viterbi has recommended a pragmatic approach with single half-rate encoder decoder for high-rate TCM codes, to achieve 2 and 6 b/s/Hz bandwid Lh efficiencies with signal constellations of 8 PSK and 256-QASK [2]. In this paper we show the performance of rate 2/3 8-state 8-PSK pragmatic codes in both linear Gaussian and band-limited non-linear satellite channel and how the various code generators of low-state single half-rate encoder structure ( whereby the higher rate pragmatic code encoder is built upon ) affect their performance.

articleTitle: Grounding System Design For An Underground Hydro-electric Plant - A Case Study
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Design of a grounding system for a hydro-electric plant located in high resistivity hill cavity and with limited available space is presented in this paper. Penstock and ground conductors laid along various tunnels are made part of the grounding system. Both analog and digital modelling techniques are used for design of the grounding system. Values of ground resistance and surface potentials, measured after the execution of the project are reported.

articleTitle: Selection of Mapping Function for Optimal Enhancement Using Fuzy Set Theoretic Measure
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Algorithm for selection of mapping function appropriate for object enhancement of a given image is described. The algorithm does not need iterative visual interaction and prior knowledge of image statistics in order to select the transformation function for its optimal enhancement. Quantitative measure for evaluating enhancement quality has been provided based on fuzzy Geometry. The concept of minimizing fuzziness (ambiguity) in both grayness and in spatial domain, as used by Pal and Rosenfeld [4], has been adopted.

articleTitle: ISDN Testing and Validation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: With the availability of standards on narrow band lSDN, telecom administrations are in the process of implementing ISDN services. Testing and validation of ISDN is a major component of this exercise. The paper identifies the various functional aspects of Basic Access narrow band lSDN testing, the tools required to implement this testing and highlights the issues requiring particular attention.

articleTitle: Performance Of Conventional Power System Stabilizers In A Series Compensated Transmission System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper deals with the analysis of dynamic stability of a single machine connected to an infinite bus through a series compensated transmission line, considering conventional Power System Stabilizers. Investigations reveal that the optimum PSS parameters obtained for light or nominal loading conditions remain practically unchanged with compensation. However, under heavy operating loads, they need be reset for compensated system. The nominal optimum PSS gives satisfactory dynamic performance for operating ranges around and below the nominal and this performance is practically unaffected by the degree of compensation.

articleTitle: Robust Controller And Observer Design For A Two-terminal HVDC System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper discusses the design of a discrete-time state feedback controller for the robust control of a two-terminal HVDC system. For a coordinated control of a two-terminal HVDC system, the rectifier current controller requires the knowledge about the inverter current. A reduced order observer is proposed in this paper which needs only the measurements of the rectifier terminal quantities, The observed quantities are then used in a state feedback controller which places the closed-loop poles in a desired way. The proposed controller structure is verified through digital computer simulation studies.

articleTitle: Updating problem in semantic data models
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Semantic data models offer a rich set of abstraction mechanisms (e.g. generalization, aggregation and classification) to database designers to explicitly specify relationships amongst objects in a database system. Some of them also allow the definition of new relationships amongst objects. This results in a situation that the existences of and/or values of attributes of objects are highly depend on that of the other objects. For example, the deletion of one object may cause the deletion of other objects. Thus, updating must be carefully handled; otherwise, the database will be led into an inconsistent state. In this paper, the approaches taken by several semantic data models in handling updating are investigated; they include: functional data models, highly structured models, models focus on dynamic, and theory oriented models. Three distinct approaches in handling the updating problem are observed and discussed. To put semantic data model into a practical use, the execution of update operations must be under control.

articleTitle: The optimal-morphological-=basis switching algorithm
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Designing optimal morpholgical filters, even in the binary case, involves a time-consuming search procedure that, in practice, can be intractable. The present paper provides an algorithm for filter design that is based upon the relationship between the optimal morphological filter and the conditional expectation. A morphological filter may not exist for a given conditional probability distribuition. If one exists, the algorithm determines the filter, optimal among morphological and other filters, almost instantaneously. If not, it changes the probability ensuring minimum increase in mean square error and determines the optimal morphological filter.

articleTitle: A New Zero Voltage Switching High Frequency Dc-to-dc Converter
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new zero voltage switching(ZVS) dc/dc converter is proposed, which provides ZVS conditions to secondary rectifying diodes as well as primary main devices. As a result of very low switching loss, the proposed converter can be operated at megahertz frequency range. The operational principle and analysis are described and verified with 150 watts prototype converter in the frequency range around a megahertz.

articleTitle: Direct Data Transfer Between Two Remote Imass Storage Devices Over A T1 Line
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A novel microprocessor-based system that acts as a serial interfaco, between a mass storage device and a high speed communication line is described. This systen-, can effectively replace the functions of a mainframe cornputermd its associated front-end processor, in bulk file transfer between two remote mass slora e devices. As a result, it provides a highly cost efficient means for remote backup and electronic offsite storage that co-aid greatly enhance the data processing centers' disaster recovery-plans. The system consists of two microprocessors, interface logic, memory, and communication controller. It converts parallel data available at the interface of the mass storage device into serial format with SDLC protocol which is ready to be transmitted over serial communication facilities having speeds up to the TI transmission rate of 1.544 Mbps. Details of the s-ystem's hardware and software design will be discussed and experimental result on a prototype system will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of an Optimum Flight Control System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents optimum AutoPilot Designs for bank-to-turn CLOS (BTT) guidance. BTT is capable of producing higher lift-to-drag ratio. Linear quadratic optimal technique is used in this paper for the design of the roll and pitch autopilot. Simulation results have demonstrated the improvements in control with the linear quadratic optimal design.

articleTitle: An Efficient Direct Cut Set Algorithm For Power System Network Reliability Evaluation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Enumeration of all minimal cut sets is an Amportant problem in power system network reliability studies. In this paper, an efficient direct algorithm for the generation of system minimal cut sets is developed. This does not require generation of minimal paths. All minimal cut sets of each load point can be easily deduced from these system minimal cut sets, Necessary computations for both load point and system reliability indices can be carried out only once using system minimal cut sets unlike in an existing method.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an ATM Artificial Traffic Generator
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper gives the description and analysis of a specific system capable of producing artificial ATM traffic under user-defined statistics. The proposed system is described in terms of its high level block diagram and a suitable queueing model is presented. The problem of properly simulating the statistical behaviour of the arrival process is discussed. The system is modeled in terms of a G/G/1 queue, whose arrival rate is not afways lower than its service rate. The transient behaviour of the queueing model is studied by using an analytical approach, which is then validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Comparative Simulation of a Threshold-Based Congestion Avoidance in Broadband ISDNs
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We present a comparative simulation of a threshold-based congestion avoidance in Broadband Integrated Services Digital Networks (B-ISDNS). Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) has been recommended by CCITT as one of the most promising means of providing efficient and fast packet switched communication among B-ISDN users. Although B-ISDNS will have an enormous amount of resources offered by fiber optics, congestion may still be experienced due to statistical variations and burstiness in arrival patterns of information traffic. The study presented in this paper deals with congestion avoidance in B-ISDNS and evaluate perfomlance of these techniques by using simulation. Simulation results are presented in the form call blocking probabilities, in comparative terms.

articleTitle: An Effective AGC For Minimizing The Accumulation Of The Time Error And Inadvertent Interchange
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper deals with Automatic Generation Control of a two equal area reheat thermal system provided with integral type supplementary controllers. A modified quadratic performance index based on area control errors, time error accumulation and inadvertent interchange has been proposed for optimizing integral gain setting of the conventional supplementary controllers. Investigations reveal that the transient as well as the steady state accumulation in time error and inadvertent interchange are considerably reduced with the optimum integral gain setting using modified performance index than using conventional performance index for both with and without generation rate constraint (GRC).

articleTitle: Implementation of OSI-IP router for LAN-LAN interconnection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: An implementation of a router with a capability to dynamically upgrade its routing table based on ISO 8473 and ISO 9542 standards is described. It is suited for use in OSI CLNS networks similar to US GOSIP recommendations. It is being proposed to use this router as a parallel stack in an existing TCP/IP router so that both OSI and TCP/IP network services can be supported over a campus wide network.

articleTitle: A New Gate Drive Circuit For MOSFETs Switching At Low Frequency
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new gate drive circuit, with ferrite core transformer isolation, for power MOSFETs switching at low frequency in the micro Hertz range has been presented. The technique involves periodic refreshing of charge on the effective gate source capacitance of the MOSFET in order to ensure low ON-state resistance, R (ON), by maintaining its gate-source voltage above the threshold level. The simulation of the drive circuit using circuit analysis program PSPICE is described with results and relevant waveforms.

articleTitle: Predictive Control Of Blast Furnaces
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A model based control strategy for a blast furnace is proposed. To implement this control strategy four submodels for the system (i) charge calculation model (ii) charge distribution model (iii) silicon prediction model and (iv) stove control model are required. The paper reports on development of the first three models and model verification against plant data from Bhilai Steel Plant.

articleTitle: Impulse Response of an Ultrasonic Imaging Scheme that Uses Frequency Modulated Pulses
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: An imaging scheme to generate B-scan ultrasound images using frequency modulated (FM) pulses, has been outlined. A prototype experimental setup is used to perform simple imaging tasks in attenuating and non-attenuating medium. The past processing of the acquired data was carried out digitally. The objective was to study the two-dimentaional point spread function as a function of the FM pulse parameters.

articleTitle: A Fast Algorithm For Alleviation Of Voltage Insecurity
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a fast method for voltage monitoring and control in the power system network. The method is based on the principle of uniqueness of solution of nonlinear reactive power balance equations and does not require the load flow solutions and system linearizations inherent in conventional approaches. The method involves calculation of new indicators (referred as D-vector in the paper) to predict under voltage or over voltage conditions and suggests the control actions to regain the predisturbance voltage profile or the new target voltage values. The method has been tested an IEEE-14 bus system and is found to be quite effective.

articleTitle: Terminal-based models for detecting winding faults in three-phase transformers
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents two electromagnetic models of three-phase transformers. the models are used to develop digital algorithms for detecting winding faults in three-phase tranmsformers. The algorithms use voltage and current measurements taken at the transformer terminals. The performance of algorithms is checked using data recorded in the Electrical Engineering Laboratories of the University of Saskatchewan. Some test results are included in the paper.

articleTitle: Design of a multilayered OSI system
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In order to realise the objectives of OSI, it needs to be implemented in a wide variety of systems. The OSI Reference model provides a lot of freedom to the implementor in realising the individual layers and in structuring the overall system. This paper presents a design strategy for the complete system and discusses some implementation options in the Transport protocol (class 4) which can enhance the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Optimum nonconcurrent digital multi-h signaling
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The problem of nonconcurrent detection of multi-h CPM signals received over AWGN channel is considered. Receiver structures for show- and fast-fading cases are presented. Employing the well known union and Average Matched Filter (AMF) bounds the error rate performance of the optimum noncoherent receiver is estimated. Through minimization of these bounds optimum multi-h schemes are determined. The results reveal that there seems to be no apparent advantage in power in going for multi-h schemes relative to single-h schemes for the case of noncoherent detection.

articleTitle: CQNET - A Package for Performance Analysis of Closed Queueing Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper an approximate procedure for the performance analysis of closed queueing networks with N stations and K total jobs is developed and discussed. Each station has a single server and an exponentially distributed service time with mean value 1/spl mu/i ( far i= 1,2,3 . . ..N ). The service discipline is based on First Come First served scheduling. To avoid deadlock, an assumption is made such that the total number of jobs in the network at any time may not exceed the total capacity of the network. The procedure so developed studies the behaviour of the system. By increasing the number of Jobs in the entire network various performance measurements are made. Comparison of the results obtained by the approximation method with the exact results demonstrates that the approximate method has reasonable accuracy.

articleTitle: Performance Of A Separately Excited DC Motor Fed From A Multiphase Chopper
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A dc chopper is normally employed for the speed control of a dc motor (separately excited or series) by varying the armature voltage. The output voltage and current of chopper possess harmonics, which affect the performance of the motor to a large extent. Current Limit Control when employed requires high frequency switching to limit the ripple to a desired extent. This switching introduces switching losses and requires the thyristors of very small turn off time. A Time Ratio Control on the other hand requires a large inductance to reduce harmonics and also to reduce the discontinuous conduction. A Multiphase Chopper where several choppers are operated in parallel with a phase shift is very effective in reducing the ripple content of voltage waveform and improving the performance of the dc motor. Further the system will be advantageous for large power applications with good reliability and without the need for operating the devices in parallel thereby increasing the device capability. The present paper deals with the analysis of a separately excited dc motor when fed from two choppers with a phase shift, operating from a dc supply. A Simple and eminent approach based on the state Space model of the do motor is presented. The effect of variation of the phase shift between the choppers on the performance of the dc motor is investigated in detail. The improvement in the performance is found to be very good even at small switching frequency.

articleTitle: Spectral estimation of short segments of EEG signals using least squares waveshaping filters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG), the manifestations of brain's electrical activity as recorded on the scalp, has become an indispensable tool in clinical neurophysiology and related fields. The main objective of EEG signal analysis is to extract valid in formation from EEG-records and for this purpose many analysis techniques have been used. As far as background activity is concerned, spectral analysis is important to determine the rhythms present. Often short segments of data is to be analysed in order to adequately characterise the temporally rapid changes that occur in EEG. This paper is concerned with this aspect of EEG analysis viz., spectral estimation of short segment EEG data. Autore gressive (AR) spectral estimation techniques are known to provide better resolution than classical periodogram methods when short segments of data are selected for analysis. We suggest in this paper a method which works better than the normal AR spectral estimation for very short segments of data. It has been observed that the energy in the EEG data segment is concentrated not in the beginning but somewhere in between the initial and the final positions thus confirming the fact that EEG is a mixed delay signal. This position where the energy is concentrated has been obtained with the help of least squares waveshaping filter. It is also shown that the knowledge of the position where the energy in the signal is concentrated can be used in making a better spectral estirna tion of short segments of EEG data. The study has been made first with the simulated data and then with the actual EEG data. It is also observed that the performance of the present method and AR method become comparable as the length of data segment increases.

articleTitle: Compressing the composite digital television signal by encoding tbe sub-bands
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper investigates a sub-band coding scheme to reduce the transmission bandwidth of the digitized composite television images. The composite signal is decomposed into seven bands. Each band is then independently encoded. The base band is DPCM encoded and the high bands are encoded by using non-uniform Laplacian quantizers with a dead zone. By selecting the dead zone on the basis of energy in the high bands an acceptable image quality is achieved at an average of 1.3028 bpp and at an average SNR of 35.02 dB. This rate is comparable to some very hardware intensive schemes of transform conipression or vector quantization proposed in the literature. The sub-band coding scheme used in this study is considered to be of medium complexity.

articleTitle: Modelization and Three-Dimensional Visulation of the Carpus From CT Slices
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a method of 3D modelization of the bones of the carpus from a set of CT slices. This modelization allows to process a 3D segmented visualization of the wrist. Many authors have studied the way of computing images of 3D data by so called "volume rendering" or "ray tracing" techniques [6, 7]. The major drawback of these approaches is that they cannot process independently the different objects appearing in the volume. Our method separates the bones of the wrist, allowing to render surfaces hidden by other bones or to evaluate precisely the location and the shape of a fracture. This technique of visualization is based on a first step of modelization of the bones. In order to isolate the bones one from the other, we apply a segmentation technique to the set of slices, producing a set of contours. To classify these contours into different bones, we use a proximity criterion based on the computation of their best approximation ellipses which allows to build an adjacence graph of the contours. Then, a bone is modelized as a connex component of this graph. This gives a wireframe representation of the bones. The external surfaces can then be approximated by triangulation or spline interpolation and visualized by classical rendering algorithms.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Class of Hybrid Token-CSMA/CD Protocols
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A class of multiple access protocols named the reserve-k hybrid token-CSMA/CD protocols are analyzed. These protocols are suitable for slotted bus-structured LAN with dynamic traffic loads. By reserve-k it is meant that the first k time slots after the channel changes state from busy to idle are reserved for the priority user. Numerical results show that the reserve-k hybrid protocols perform as good as the better of the control token and the CSMA/ CD protocoIs at all times. Besides, it is found that k = 1 is the best choice among the class of investigated protocols.

articleTitle: Requency Domain Design Of Digital Controllers
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new frequency-domain method of designing digital controllers for single-input single-output systems in proposed in this paper. The objective is to design a digital controller such that the response of the resulting closed loop system matches approximately a specified response.The method uses the principle of approximate model matching in the Pade sense and leads to linear algebraic oquations in the unknown controller parameters. One illustrative example compares this method with several digital control algorithms.

articleTitle: A Temporal Logic over Partial Orders for Analysis of Real-Time Properties of Distributed Programs
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Temporal logic is widely acclaimed to be a highly successful tool for analyzing non-real-time properties of programs. However, a few fundamental problems arise while designing temporal logic-based-techniques to verify real-time properties of programs. in this context, we formulate a modal logic called distribued logic (DL) by using ideas from both the interleaving and partial ordering approach. This logic uses spatial modal operators in addition to temporal operators for representing real-timed concurrency. In addition to the syntax and semantics of the logic, programming model and a formal proof technique based on the logic are also presented. Finally, use of the proof method is illustrated through the analysis of the real-time properties of a generic multiproceess producer/consumer program.

articleTitle: Finding strongly connected components in series parallel graphs
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We present an efficient parallel algorithm which finds the strongly connected components of a series-parallel digraph. The algorithm ruris in O(log/sup 2/n) time and uses O(n) processors. As a consequence, the reachability problern can be solved efficiently for series parallel digraphs in O(log/sup / n) parallel time us ing O(n) number of processors.

articleTitle: Three-level Control Scheme For Load-frequency Control Of Interconnected Power Systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a decentralized control technique for the Load-Frequency Control (LFC) of a single area multimachine power system. This technique is evolved from a three-level hierarchical scheme which successfully converts the LFC problem into an interactive proess. The decentralized computation is carried out both horizontally by generating a group of local decoupled optimization subproblems, and vertically through the division of the coordination task into two nested optimization processes. The former ensures that the optimal local subproblems are satisfied and hence, yields the local optimum solutions. The latter takes into account system nonlinearities and interconnections art d ensures that the performance of the overall system is optimized. This paper differs from previous works in that the proposed technique is fast and simple, and permits optimality at all the levels while providing a decomposed solution. Moreover, the proposed scheme guarantees practically zero steady-state error in both frequency and tie-line power at the final time.

articleTitle: Importance Of Generation Scheduling Of Thermal Units For Economic Operation Of Power Systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The demand for electrical power is growing rapidly due to industrialisation and the utilities are not in a position to plan their generation capacity additions suitably to meet this growing demand for power. This has resulted in a large gap between generation and demand. In this context, economical operation of the system, so as to utilise the capacities optimally become very important. This can be achieved by suitably scheduling the thermal generating units and committing them appropriately, for a projected load demand on the system, arrived at, using short term load forecasting techniques.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Based Critic For Evaluation Of Architectural floor-plans
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Critiquing is the process of providing reasoned opinion on an object. it is essential as a supplementary problem solving activity in any co-operative problem solving environment to provide selective portions of knowledge to the u@ers In the form of "why not" kind of explanations. In this article, we discuss about CAFE - a knowledge based Critic for Architectural Floor-plan Evaluation. It provides textual-criticism by evaluating floor-plans of residential buildings with respect to different factors of function-utility, basic planning principles and client expectations. Floor-plan evaluation is a complex task that requires to model different components of knowledge there is a need to handle abstractions and the problem solving behavior required by the critic is quite; complex requiring a dynamic agenda based approach that allows identification of goals from the given situation. This forms the motivation for building a knowledge based system for It. We discuss in detail about this system CAFE, the underlying assumptions, types of critic rules handled, knowledge representation and the problem solving scheme followed. We also present a typical scenario with CAPE. Finally, we analyze the system and propose extensions.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of the AP and the SSC and design of the system overload controls of India's C-DOT digital switching system
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Government of India's Centre for Development of Telernatics (C DoT) has developed a modular, distributed telephone switching system. There is an ongoing effort to model, analyse, and optirnise the teletraffic performance of this switching system. In this paper we report the methodology and results of a part of this work. We use analytical queuing models to estimate the capacities of the Administrative Processor, and the Space Switch Controller. We formulate the system overload control problem as a constrained optimisation problem, solve the problem, and use simulations to evaluate various adaptive overload control algorithms.

articleTitle: A Suite of Software Tools for Executing Formal Specifications
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a suite of tools that have been implemented - to facilitate the execution of formal specifications written in the non-executable Z language. Such tools assist the system developer towards ensuring whether the functional requirements as specified (in Z) are reflected in the implementation (in Prolog). The specification technique used in this work is explained with an example specification. The transformation of some Z specifications into Prolog are provided using our development environment. The limitations of our approach and further work in this area are addressed.

articleTitle: Object oriented approach for information systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Object oriented approach in analysing, designing, and developing complex systems offers significant benefits such as; natural and consistent decomposition of an application, powerful means for controlling access to a shared database, data abstraction, structural knowledge representation, and reusability. In this paper, we will define the concepts and clarify the terms used to describe the various aspects of object oriented approach; present an object oriented model and discuss its characteristics; demonstrate the application of object oriented approach with an example of a manufacturing company; and discuss some of the research issues that need to be addressed in object oriented systems.

articleTitle: AI Approach to Hand Written Devnagiri Script Recognition
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, a system for recognizing hand written Indian Devnagiri script has been proposed. This system uses an AI approach to integrate information from diverse sources. It has three levels of abstraction low, medium and high. At each level of abstraction, knowledge appropriate to that level is used to identfy the components of the higher level concept. At low level of abstraction, a given document is segmented into components, at the meduim level features are extracted from the segment, and at the high level segments are reconized with available contextual the help of information. To deal with imprecise information a new approach based on the fuzzy logic concept has been suggested.

articleTitle: On Ultimate Boundedness Control Of Uncertain Dynamical Systems Using The Adaptive Bound On The Uncertainty
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We consider a class of uncertain dynamical systems containing uncertain elements without a priori information except that they are bounded. In deterministic design of feedback controllers for such systems, bounds on the uncertainties are an important clue to guarantee the asymptotic stability or uniform ultimate boundedness of the closed-loop system. But, sometimes these bounds may not be easily obtained because of the complexity of structure of the uncertainties. In this paper, based on the estimation of the bound of the uncertainties, we propose an adaptive control which renders the uncertain dynamical systems uni formly ultimately bounded.

articleTitle: Trade-Off Between Time Complexity and Accuracy of Perceptron Learning /sup */
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, a modified perception leaning algorithm is proposed to reduce the computation time of learning. The proposed algorithm is easily programmed and can drastically decrease the time complexity of learning at the expense of only a little accuracy. Experimental results further show that this trade is worthy. Our proposed modified perceptron learning learning is then practical especially when noise exists in the training set or when the requirement of computational time is critical.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Steady State Heat Conduction Moblems By Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A three dimensional finite element solution of the heat conduction problem is described. The shape functions and exact solution matrices are derived algebrically for utmost economy in computation. The method of application to the heat flow problem first to a simple cylinder and then to the stator of an induction motor is indicated.

articleTitle: High speed in-circuit emulator for 8039 microcomputer
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: An 8039/49 single chip microcomputer based 'High speed in-circuit emulator is presented here.The single chip microcomputers distinguish themselves from microprocessors by the fact that they have their memory-ROM & RAM and their Input/Output ports integrated on the chip itself emulator presented here (USE- 49)allows you to run user programs on the microcomputer chip for which they have been designed, at any time in the development cycle. You can run and debug a software program on USE-49 emulator before user hardware is available.

articleTitle: A Stable Model Reference Adaptive Control System with a Priori Knowledge About Plant Parameter
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A Parameter adaptive algorithm,suitable for direct Parameter discrete time model reference adaptive control system with a priori knowledge about the plant parameter variations is proponed.This algorithm is based on Lyapunov's stability theory and additionally with prior! informations of the plant parameter variations.There are many instances where all the plant Parameters donot vary.In -such situations fast adaptation and added stability can be achieved by giving zero weightage to the corresponding controller parameters. Therefore stability of the system in the z-plane and perfomance of convergence is more guaranteed.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Protective-engineering-for Industrial Power System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Well co-ordinated protective relaying enhances the reliability of large Induestrial Power Systems which may be quite complex with inplant captive power generation operating in parallel with utility grid. The task of protection co-ordination with time graded overcurrent protective relays of various characteristics can be simplified with application of computer graphics. This paper deals with such a software developed for computer aided protection co-ordination.
