articleTitle: Asynchronous SIMD Architecture for Image Processing
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The Asynchronous SIMD architecture is presented as an alternative to a normal SIMD architecture. The asynchronous SIMD architecture uses a Global Control Unit an array of processors ( each equipped with local memory and a control unit ) and an interconnection network. The architecture operates in two modes - the Configuration mode (during which the global control unit broadcasts instructions and the processors store the instructions in the local memories ) and the Execution Mode ( during which the processors execute the instructions stored in the local memories ) . The benefits obtained from the architecture are studied. lmage processing is identified as a target application area.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Controller For A Seperately Excited D.C. Motor
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper describes the application of fuzzy logic to the speed control of d.c. motor. A generallsed rule structure is used to develop change in the control strategy & response for various conditions are discussed. Results indicate that FLC works well even with inaccurate data; Optimum error performance can be obtained by proper selection of quantization levels, sampling interval, etc.

articleTitle: Identification Of Continuous-time MIMO Systems From Noisy Data
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Two algorithms for the identification of linear time-invariant multivariable continuous-time systems with input and noisy output data are presented in this paper. Orthogonal transformations like Householder transformations and plane rotations are used and the system is identified in the form of a state-variable model.

articleTitle: Unlearning in Feed-Forward Neural Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We present two algorithms for unlearning an already stored pattern in feed- forward neural networks. The proposed algorithms are modifications of the backpropagation method. The method will find applications whenever the training set has to be updated frequently. The proposed algorithms have the propery that the retrieval of other pattens are not affected due to the selective unlearning.

articleTitle: An Implementation of PARLOG for Shared-Memory Multiprocessor Environment
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper we present an implementation of PARLOG under a multi-processor operating system and the semantics of the synchronization primitives used by the implementation. Moreover, aself-scheduling algorithm for PARLOG programs is also described The implementation, a source-to-source transformation, generates machine-independent parallel C-code. The Threads-back-bone package provides the required concurrent environment and the various parallel constructs. The two-phase transition scheme provides the possibility of incorporating various machine-independent optirnizations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Two Discrete-time HVDC Converter Models
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper describes the development of discrete-time six pulse HVDC converter models for small signal stability analysis and controller design. Assuming that the converter firing and the end of commutation period as two discrete time instants, a suitable linearized converter model is then interfaced with a current controller and an R-L load to determine the overall system model. Two separate, but similar, methods are used to find the system model. They are state space model with cyclic rate sampling and transfer function model derived using the modified-z transform. The models are then studied through their the stability boundaries and root loci and are verified through digital computer simulation.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Based Dielectric Oil Testing
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Dielectric strength of an insulating oil is an important parameter, while it is being used as a transformer oil. It is determined by its capability of withstanding the highest voltage without breakdown under specified conditions. The paper presents the microprocessor based dielectric oil testing, which facilitates many advantages such as reliability, flexibility etc.

articleTitle: Image convolver - design of an ASIC chip
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Design of a convolver chip operating in real time has been reported here. The chip yields normalised convolved outputs for 3 x 3 convolution and may be extended for 5 x 5 convolution also for image processing applications. The architecture is modular and suitable for VLSI implementation. The design has been carried out using VTI ASIC design tools and simulation results have been shown.

articleTitle: A fast fault simulator for sequential logic circuits
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The P-model approach of modelling a combinational digital circuit using Petri nets has been introduced in [1]. Based on the P-model representation, the present paper introduces an efficient fault simula tor design for synchronous sequential circuits. The method consists in partitioning a given circuit into disjoint fanout-free regions (FFRs), translating each FFR into P-model, applying minimizing transforma tions, and performing fault simulation on the minimized FFRs. This technique is expected to be faster as compared to existing fault simu lation techniques.

articleTitle: Adaptive relaying concepts for generator protection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Adaptive relaying concepts as applicable to generator protection are presented in this paper. Adaptive relaying deploys changes in relaying settings and/or change in relay characteristics or even a change in relaying modus operandi as and when the system configuration or oprating conditions change. This type of adaptive relaying improves system response and performance. Adaptive relaying principles presented tacitly assumes that the system id equipped with digital relays that work via minicomputer based facility.

articleTitle: Recent Trends In Power System Protection
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The recent trend in protection has been a shift to Numerical Protection Techniques, thanks to the development of single chip digitaI signal pracessiors with high number crunching capability, which has made it possible to design digital filters in real time. In the Protection field, Numerical techniques have first found application to Line Protection, and allid c ompIementary functions Iike Fault Locator, Disturbance Recorder and Autoreclosing. Numerical Transformer Protection has also been developed, and research is going on for the development of a Numerical Bus Bar Protection. This paper describes the salient features of the latest State-of-the-art Numerical Distance Relay type RELZ 100, and Numerical Disturbance Recorder type REOR. The first, and the major part, cover s RELZ 100. The Input Unit, Measuring Unit and the various Options are explained. In the second part, certain details of the Disturbance Recorder REOR, ard Autorelose Relay REXA are explained.

articleTitle: Designing Systolic Arrays for Image Processing using the Recursive Replacement Scheme
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The concept of designing systolic arrays by recursively replacing its modules by one or more scaled down versions of the original systolic array, is explained. The recursive replacement scheme is applied to design efficient systolic arrays for solving matrix-based problems used in Image Processing. Different performance measurement parameters are defined to study performance benefits.

articleTitle: Experiences in Design, Engineering, Implementation and operation of DCS Based C&I System for Trombay 500 MW Unit No. 6
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper describes the experiences gained by Tata Electric Companies Bombay, India on the Distributed Digital control system (DCS) based C&I system for their 500 MW Unit at Trombay (Unit-6), over a period of four years through key phases of the project viz. (a) Design Conceptualisation (b) Detailed Engineering and System Implementation and (c) Unit synchronisation and first year of operation. The problems encountered at various phases of the project and their resolution have been highliqhted.

articleTitle: A Simple Indirect Method For Decoupling Control Of Current-Fed Induction Motor And A Compensation Scheme For Rotor Resistane Variation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Operation of an induction motor under indirect field oriented control is highly parameter sensitive, and is thus susceptible to the loss of decoupling between the flux and torque producing components of the stator current vector resulting in the performance degradation under both steady state and dyna mic conditions. One of the most influencing parameters is the rotor resistance whose variation is caused by change in operating temperature. A simple method of adapting for rotor resistance change, based on the generation of an ideal reference for quadrature axis current from do link power measure ment is suggested in this paper. The control scheme involves no coordinate transformation. The validity of the proposed method is confirmed by digital computer simulation. The simulation results consider the dynamics of the induction motor with changed rotor resistance, current controller and field oriented controllers and show that the rotor resistance can be estimated with reasonable accuracy even in the transient state, and the decoupling operation of the induction motor can be maintained.

articleTitle: A new allgorithm for finding all tekks consisting of some nodes in a graph
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for finding all trees called as INTERESTED TREES consisiting of some specified nodes called INTERESTED NODES in a graph.

articleTitle: An Optimal Systolic Solution to the Two-Dimensional Discrete Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A Parallel Fault Simulator on a Multiprocessor
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The present paper reports the outcome of an effort to implement the concurrent fault simulation [ Ulrich 1973] algorithm on a transputer based multiprocessor. The algorithm as implemented have been run on several ISCAS benchmark circuits [Brglez 1985] and the performance with regards to speedup and efficiency evaluated.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Strip Breakage for 5-Stand Tandem Mill
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Strip Breakage in tandem cold rolling process causes damages to work toll, mill equipment and more mill down time. Automatic detection of breakage and stopping of mill helps in minimising these problems. Most of the tandem mill with conventional control system does not support strip breakage detection logic. This paper describes a simple and reasonably successful way for automatic detection of strip breakage between any pair of Stands. The proposed detection logic has been realised with - roll forces, stand speeds, inter-stand tensions, motor armature currents and exit gauge. It detects the strip breakage during metal threading, constant rolling and trailing out of metal. The application software also collects pre and post breakage data and generates report at the end of shift.

articleTitle: Transformation Based Fast Decoupled Loadflow
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a Transformation based Fast Decoupled Loadflow method along with a simple modification of real power mismatches at PV-nodes. Rotation angles are limited to the maximum value of -36/spl deg/. Also suggested is the slack-start procedure for efficiency. The method is tested and compared with the recent General-purpose version of the Fast Decouplod Loadflow (GFDL) method under wide range of simulated circumstances of system operating conditions and network parameters. The proposed method is in general better convergent and it can be more than twice as fast as the GFDL method for systems of large R/X ratio branches.

articleTitle: Gas Insulated Substations in India- An Overview
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: Improved Distortion Measures for Image Vector Quantization
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The role played by the distortion measure in a vector quantization image encoder is very important. In the following paper we suggest a general class of distortion function, the input-dependent weighted square error distortion, which is computationally simple and can be used to incorporate some psychovisual characteristics. Two techniques of using this distortion function have been discussed. Incorporating various classes depending on image activity in the distortion measure, better subjective quality can be achieved without added complexity, as our simulation studies have shown. This strategy of classified codebook is optimal and more general than the conventional subcodebook method. We also show that incorporating dimensional emphasis, blocklness can of marginally more computation.

articleTitle: The Analysis Of Random Sequential Faults On A Multiphase Generator
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A complicated sequential fault on a multiphase power system may involve grounding of some phases, short circuit between some phases in one or more bunches and isolation of some phases. All these faults may take place in any sequence. This paper presents a generalized method for analysing such faults. Two matrices which may be called 'the terminal voltage co-efficient matrix' and 'the ground fault co-efficient matrix' are employed for the analysis. The elements of these matrices can immediately be written for any state of the system. The method presented imposes no restriction either on the sequence in which the complicated fault develops or on the instants on the voltage waves at which the faults develop. Actual phase variables are employed for the analysis and expressions for transient phase currents, transient terminal voltages and the transient neutral current are given. By suitably adjusting certain constants and the summation indices in the general expressions, the method can be applied to an n-phase power system. As an application of the proposed method, the results for an arbitrary sequential fault on a six phase system are given.

articleTitle: Sampled Data Automatic Generation Control Of A Two Area Reheat Thermal System With Modified Area Control Error
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper deals with Automatic Generation Control (AGC) of a two area reheat thermal system with modified area control error (ACEM) considering operation of the system in the continuous-mode and that of the controller in the discrete mode. ACEM is the weighted sum of frequency deviation, tie-power deviation and inadvertent interchange energy. Studies show that the AGG-strategy based on ACEM provides constancy of frequency and tie-power flow, zero steady state error in inadvertent interchange energy and negligible error in time error accumulation in the steady state. Further the dynamic responses of the system obtained with controllers based on ACEM are close to the.responses based on new area control error ( ACEN - Ref [21] ) but are much superior to the corresponding responses achieved with controllers based on conventional area control error.

articleTitle: An interactive structured program development tool
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Efforts have been made to establish structured decision table (SDT) as an abstraction of the top-down program development methodology, by representing each step in the program development by a structured decision table and the entire process of development by a hierarchy of structured decision tables. This paper reports an interactive SDT based program development tool which facilitates top down, stepwise program development. The underlying data base stores each development steps which may be retrieved, modified and updated for program modification.

articleTitle: Geometrically continuous curve and surface generation using catmull-rom splines
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: It is reported earlier that continuously shaped Beta splines are more expensive to compute. In this paper attempt has been to develop computationaliy efficient algorithm for a class of Catmull-Rom spline using Bezier control polygon for each segment and Bernstin polynomial blending function.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Characteristics of Conflict-Free Permutations in Omega Interconnection Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: An Invariant Feature For 3-D Object Recognition
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The objective of this paper is to find translation, rotation, and magnification Invariant and unique characterization algorithms for the finite 3-dimerisional discrete objects. We introduce one unique and two pseudo characterization algorithms which are based on the notion of "distances" between the elements of the given finite 3-dimensional discrete objects and Its complement.

articleTitle: A movable user interface based on a simple x-window like protocol
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: All contemporary operating systems support a logical device name that is a synonym for the activating terminal (eg /dev/tty on UNIX, and T1. on RSX-11M+1. The startup procedures also ensure that one or more files are open to this device when any process begins execution. This mechanism has one significant limitation -- user interaction is bound to one physical terminal, and the user may not move to another without disrupting the process. This paper describes the implementation of a movable user interface (MUI) on the RSX LIM+ operating system. MUI is an environment in which a process user has unlimited flexibility of location. The terminal I/O of a process may be relocated by the user to different terminals with complete continuity. Neither the programs nor the operating system have to be modified to use MUl.

articleTitle: Computational structure of two sequential -decoding alcoriths
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Recently a modification to the conventional Fano Algorithm was suggested by-the authors [1]. This; Modified-Fano Algorithm was shown to have lesser number of computations per bit of decoding, under fixed error conditions. Simulation results of the distribution of the computation time for the two algorithms under AWGN and Raleigh fading conditions were also reported [2]. In this paper authors present the structural view of the distribution-time of the two decoders. Since the computational steps in the case of Fano and Modified-Fano algorithms remain essentially same; the computational performance of the two algorithms are tested in terms of these steps as parameters. The results obtained indicate that Modified-Fano algorithm is computationally superior in AWGN as well as Fading Channels. The Implications of looking at performance of the decoding algorithms from this angle (Structural or component wise effort of the decoders) are discussed.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Relaying System For A Power Distribution Network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes an adaptive relaying system for protecting a power distribution network using overcurrent and directional overcurrent relays. The system is designed to change, in an on-line mode, relay settings as load and generation levels change over a period of days. The system is applied to a reduced model of the 'City of Saskatoon' distribution network.

articleTitle: Interworking Plan for Business Communication Network An ISDN Experiment in India
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes the interworking arrangement between the Business Communication Network and other networks such as PSTN, PSPDN, and Telex. The Business Communication Network is an e.qrerbnental effort on ISDN in India. It is envisaged that full scale interworking with other networkr will not be practicable from the beginning. However, it is intended that the subscribers connected w BCN should be able to establish calls for Voice/Fax, Packet Data and Telex with the subscribers of PSTN, PSPDN and Telex networks respectively

articleTitle: Analysis And Damping Of Torsional Oscillations Through Supplementary Exciation Control
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The effectiveness of stabilizing signals introduced at the input of an excitation system using a power system stabilizer (PSS) is analysed to damp torsional oscillations in a series compensated system is investigated. Two methods (i) generator shaft speed deviation signal and (ii) modal speed deviation as feedback signals to PSS (a) one PSS (b) two PSS is studied.The study system (similar to second IEEE Benchmark model system I) consists of a synchronous generator connected to an infinite bus through two parallel transmission lines, one of which is series compensated. A power system stabilizer (PSS) is installed in the excitation system to provide damping torque for the generator. The PSS described here is designed to damp the torsional oscillations. Main empahsis is given on modelling aspects of PSS and its effectiveness in damping the torsional oscillations.

articleTitle: New Control Strategy For Load Frequency Control Problem
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper deals with a new control strategy of quenching transients of a load frequency problem. The load frequency problem is represented by a new state space model for a single area Electric power system. The state variables selected in this model are frequency, first and second derivatives of frequencies. The steady state operating points before and after the load disturbance are named as initial and final states of the system. Now the LFC problem is restructured as a state transition problem (initial to final states) using a suitable control parameter. With the help of Pontryagins Maximum Principle (PMP) the LFC problem is proved to be bang-bang control problem by minimizing the time of state transfer. The control parameter is taken to be the position of speed changer which is not an external parameter.

articleTitle: Estimating Performance of Mergesort on a Network of Transputers
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The estimation of the implemented behavior like execution time etc., of a parallel algorithm is a difficult task. The bound estimates may typically differ from measured parameters of an implemented algorithm by several orders of magnitude, due to the presence of a number of virtual layers between such theoretical bound models and the implemented versions. A systematic procedure for obtaining a realistic estimate of the execution time of a non-trivial parallel algorithm like mergesort is outlined in this paper. The measured hardware instruction cycles are in close agreement with the calculated theoretical instruction cycles.

articleTitle: Printed International Character Recognition
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, we investigate three geometric pattern recognition algorithms based on mathematical morphology and apply the algorithms to printed character recognition. These methods can provide an alternative way of template matching which is the most straight forward method in character recognition.

articleTitle: Obtaining A Part-based 3-D Object Representation from Range Data
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We examine two methods of obtaining a part-based 3-D object representation from range images. A small number (12) of shape types based on geolis are used as 3-D part primitives. The first method fits superquadric models to the depth data and then distinguishes between the shape classes by using statistical classifiers. Features for the classification are derived from the estimated superquadric parameters. Fairly good results are obtained using synthetic images. A second proposed method takes a differential-geometric approach. Surface segmentation of the range image is performed based on curvatures, and the part primitive is recognized based on the surface types and their adjacencies. Surfaces types and adjacencies of the part primitives also determine a small number of characteristic views to be stored in a multi-view representation of the primitives. This is to be used in cases where the surface types and adjacencies in the image yield more than one possibility for the part primitive.

articleTitle: A Technique To Improve The Convergence Of FDLF For Systems With High R/X Lines
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A technique to improve the convergence of FDLF for systems with high R/X lines has been suggested in this paper. It is proposed that a slack bus which has the minimum sum of the squares of deviations of bus voltage angles will give the better convergence properties of FDLF compared to any other bus as the slack node. This is demonstrated by taking examples of variety of systems. This technique is implemented on BX version of FDLF.

articleTitle: Comparative evaluation of Fano, stack and minimum-distance sequential decoders for forward error correction
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The three principal sequential decoding techniques : the Fano, the Stack and the minimum-distance decoding algorithms have been studied through simulation for a short constraint length. Curves for bit error rate and computational effort have been presented and a comparison is drawn.

articleTitle: Dynamics and Control Of A Pilot Scale Distillation Column
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes the development of an experimental facility of a pilot scale distillation column and the study of its dynamics and control. Pulse and step tests were carried out to obtain the transfer function models which were used in designing PID type controllers. While PI was found to be adequate for controlling top or bottom composition, this scheme did not fare well when used in a multivariable environment to control top and bottom compositions simultaneously. Single loop generalized predictive control (GPC) when used adaptively was found to be superior to PI control but not entirely satisfactory because of strong loop interaction. Preliminary simulation studies on the transfer function model showed that single variable GPC with feedforward may be the answer to this problem.

articleTitle: Design for Easy ISDN Provisioning and Maintenance
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper is aimed at bringing out the design aspects of a modern digital exchange and the Terminal Equipment (TE), which can support multiple services over the telecommunication network and has wide ranging benefits to the nerwork provider from the point of view of provisioning and maintenance.

articleTitle: Orthogonal l/sub 1/ Reconstruction Method for Computerized Tomography
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new method of image reconstruction for computerized tomography is proposed using Orthogonal l/sub 1/ techniqne. The proposed method can reconstruct the image using less number of rays. Further improvement in the reconstruction is achieved by incorporating the known a priori knowledge like normegativity, finite support, amplitude and energy bounds on the overall images.

articleTitle: Investigation Of Computatton Techniques For Simulation Of Large Scale Power System Dynamics
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes investigations towards arriving at a most suitable algorithm for real time simulation of power system dynamics. Even though the modelling and simulation aspects of real time simulation are based on ideas that have already been laid down for conventional transient stability analysis, the choice of the best algorithm for real time simulation requires different guide lines. In transient stability analysis, the stress is on accuracy. In real time simulation, computation time and numerical stability are more important. In this paper, various algorithms, obtained through different combinations of the choices of synchronous machine model, solution approach, angle corrector formula, and convergence criteria for the network solution, have been compared with respect to computation speed and solution accuracy.

articleTitle: Stabilization Of A Wind Turbine Driven Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper is concerned with the dynamic behavior of small synchronous generators suitable for use in wind energy conversion systems. A simulation example, using a 1600 kw/1800 rpm machine, illustrates the transient behavior of the synchronous generator without any supplementary stabilizer. A stabilzer is designed using an eigenvalue placement technique. Then the degree of stability is examined with the stabilizer. Variations in load are used to show performance under different operating conditions. Both small and large disturbance simulations are presented. The problem oriented language, SUPERSCEPTRE, was used for all the simulations.

articleTitle: Parallel processing of a multilayer routing package
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: With the increasing density of components on Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) and the advance ment of fabrication technologies for multilayer PCBs, improvement of speed and techniques for the Computer Aided Design of multilayer PCBs has be come a major area of research. The paper discusses the parallel processing of layering and routing algorithms for design of multilayer PCBs on a network of small computers with a moderately high speed communication medium. Multilayer PCB design consists in partitioning a netlist into as many layers as necessary, and routing one or two layersat a time. The routing processes of the different netlists is entirely independent of each other.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Intonation for Indian Languages
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, we examine the importance of intonational knowledge and its acquisition, representation and activation in an unrestricted text-to-speech system for Indian languages, particularly for Hindi. The declarative sentences in Hindi show a declining pattern of fundamental frequency (Fo) contour whereas interrogative sentences show a rising F0 contour. This backdrop declining or rising pattern is characterized by local falls and rises which are determined by the phonological pattern of the constituent words. In complex declarative sentences the declining tendency resets at syntactic boundaries. The values of resetting depends on the strength of the syntactic boundaries. Experiments on inherent F0 of segments are conducted and the contextuali variations of the segments in connected speech are analyzed. The knowledge obtained from the analysis is coded in a production system format. The intelligibility and naturalness of speech output increases after the incorporation of intonational knowledge.

articleTitle: The Performance Study of Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks using Simulations
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A Local Area Network simulation package SIMLAN has been developed to model and simulate large networks having many heterogeneous LAN segments interconnected by routers or bridges. The package is written in FORTRAN 77. It supports Token-Ring, CSMA/CD and a more recently proposed Ring/Bus protocol based networks with some of their variations. Both bridges and routers are modelled with the assumption that the packets going through them do not suffer from processing delay and there is adequate buffer for all newly arriving and backlogged packets waiting for their turn to get transmitted. A user interface is also provided to help configure the desired interconnected network for simulation runs.

articleTitle: Application Of The Homotopy Method To Finding Dispatch Solutions
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The functions of the cost curve and transmission losses are existing nonlinear, simultaneous subject to equality and inequality constraints. Mathematically, the solutions of the nonlinear equations of economic dispatch problem may result in multiple solutions, singal solution or no solution. Conventional methods may fail to find all the multiple solutions if the initial guess values are not appropriately located within the convergency region. To overcome this difficulty te homotopy method is suggested for the solution technique. In this paper the homotopy theorem is incorporated with the B-coefficient method to solve the economic dispatch problem. Not only the initial value is easily obtained but also all the multiple solutions can be obtained. So the next exact least cost of economic dispatch can be derived.

articleTitle: The Influence Of Disaggregation Applied To Time Series Modelling Of Electrictipy Demand In The Industrial Sector
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper discusses the development of time series models for manufacturing industries, and presents empirical results on the data for 18 industrial groups based on standard industrial classification (SIC)- over the period 1981 to 1989 for Northern Ireland. The derived models are then used to forecast the electricity demand for the industrial sector of a utility. The value of using disaggregate data for modelling has also been emphasised.

articleTitle: Analysis Of A Class Of PWM Sinewave Inverters With High Frequency Link
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper the salient features of four different topologies of low frequency sinewave inverter with high frequency link and PWM control is presented. The inverters employ ferrite cored transformers, inductors, resonant filters tuned to switching frequency (>20 kHZ) and power MOSFETs resulting in compact design. Equivalent circuit approach is used for analyzingall the four topologies and computer simulation. The method of synthesizing the sinusoidal PWM waveform, as well al estimation of total harmonic distortion and response of the low pass filters using discrete time domain analysis are presented along with the relevant graphs and waveforms.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of transient signal in non-Gaussian noise
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, an optimal estimator based on minimum-variance polynomial approximation is presented, which is capable of estimating the problem parameters of a transient signal in noise whose PDF may not be Gaussian. Simulation results are provided for various symmetric unimodal noise densities.

articleTitle: Research in Medical Informatics at Georgia Tech : An Overview
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The overall objective of this paper is to describe ongoing research programs in the Medical Informatics Laboratory in the Bioengineering Center of the Georgia Institute of Technology. Current research projects are highly interdisciplinary, spanning such areas as computer vision and image processing, artificial intelligence, and computer graphics and visualization. In general, the emphasis of the research programs is placed on the processing, interpretation, and display of biomedical imagery. These investigations, supported by an expanding academic program in bioengineering and performed in collaboration with medical researchers, are aimed at exploring basic issues in science and engineering while at the same time contributing practical solutions to a variety of problems in health care.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalencing And Optimal Choice Of Excitation System Parameters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A digital simulation method for selecting the optimal excitation system parameters from multi-machine dynamic stability studies is presented. A simple method using only the Y-bus matrix of the network and inertia constants and transient reactances of the machines has been used for identifying coherent machines. A dynamic equivalencing procedure is then employed for reducing the large- scale system to a reduced order system which is subsequently used for stability studies. The synchronous machines are represented by detailed five coil models. The IEEE computer simulation models for both static and brushless excitation systems have been provided in the programme. The optimal choice of the excitation system parameters is obtained by eigen value analysis of the system [A]-matrix over the full ranges of the parameters.

articleTitle: Analytical Studies Of Voltage And Current Transients During Fast Bus Transfer In A.C. Auxiliary System Of Thermal Power Station
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper presents a powerful approach to analyse the voltages and currents during auxiliary bus transfer. A generalized computer program using multi-motor modelling suitable for analysis of a number of motors connected on the unit bus has been developed. In the first part of the study, auxiliary bus voltage decay and phase angle, speed fall of various motors, motor residual voltage and current and bus frequency are investigated at discrete time interval of 0.001 second. In the second part of the study the in-rush currents in the individual motors at different instants of closing of the reserve bus are predicted. Also, the bus-voltage recovery characteristic i s obtained. A test case is also illustrated.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Model Reduction Algorithm based on Impulse-Response Grammians
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems

articleTitle: A hybrid access protocol for multiple access satelite communications network
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A new hybrid protocol for multiple access in satellite Commucations is proposed. Its stability is proved under general stationary assumptions. Also, we show the continuity of the system distributions as a function of the input distributions and obtain some stochastic comparison results. A dynamic decentralized algorithm is developed to obtain efficient partitioning of the set of users, Some simulation results are presented to demonstrate the usefulness of these algorithms.

articleTitle: Dual LMS algorithm for adaptive echo cancellation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, a simple modification of the well-known LMS algorithm, called dual LMS (DLMS) algorithm, is proposed for adaptive echo cancellation. The new algorithm operates as if two LMS algorithms are working in a cascaded manner, where the transition threshold between the two LMS algorithms and their step sizes are optimally chosen to yield the most rapid convergence under an initial and desired residual echo. As compared to the original LMS algorithm, the DLMS algorithm offers much better convergence performance and retains the advantage of hardware simplicity. Computer simulation is employed to show the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: The Mixed Queues Arising in Overflow Models
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper present an advanced method for traffic analysis of communication network.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation Of Progressive Image Transmission Techniques
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Progressive image transmission is receiving attention for application in interactive image communication over low-bandwidth channels. In progressive image transmission (PIT), a low radiation image is first transmissions until the received image is reasonably a good representation of the original image.

articleTitle: Design of IIR filters using a new transformation based on non-Taylor discretization
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A differential.equation is replaced by difference equation in discrete systems based on Taylor series approximation. Here a superior non-Taylor approximation is used to develop a new transformation and IIR filters have been designed. The performances of such filters have been compared with those based on bilinear transformation.

articleTitle: An Efficient Radiation Treatment of a Brain Tumor
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper provides a highly efficient radiation treatment method that would maximize the effect or radiation in tumor regions and minimize the radiation on normal tissues. To present an algorithm for the development of an efficient radiation treatment system, the paper addresses three problems, namely identification of three dimensional boundaries of the brain and the tumor, decomposition of the tumor into a minimal number of spheres that would cover only the tumor without any gap, and computation of optimal radioactive paths for each of these spheres.

articleTitle: Simulation and Performance Evaluation of High Performance Fibre Optic Bus Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Evaluation of wide spectrum of performance parameters of few contemporary, high-speed fibre optic bus networks has been made through simulation. Important features of the simulation procedure adopted are accommodation of variable transmission rate, variable packet size, variable generation rate, and differential delay estimation for the networks. A comparative study of the protocols used in the networks is presented.

articleTitle: Determination Of The First Swing Stability By Solving Simultaneous Differential And Algebraic Equation Set Without System Reduction
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a method for analysing the first swing stability by solving simultaneous differential and algebraic equation set in time domain without system reduction. The CPU time required by the proposed method, which is always the first consideration in fast transient stability assessment, is less than the contemporary methods including various techniques based on Lyapunov's Direct method. The significant advantage of this method is, furthermore, that it can incorporate various modeling requirements, such as successive contingent events, the different synchronous machine model applicable for the first swing analysis, the effect of loads, as well as automatic control operations.

articleTitle: Prototyping of Lotos Specifications in Functional Languages
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: We discuss how a higher-order, purely functional, modular programming language with processes and networks can be used to clescribe LOTO S constructs and specifications. First we give a short introduction to A (Applicative ), the functional notation used. Then we proceed to show how the constructors used in LOTOS specifications can be implemented in the functional notation. The article finishes with a discussion on the practical exercises we have undertaken.

articleTitle: Parallel Process Placement from Funtional Prototype Instrumentation
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Functional prototypes may be translated into imperative parallel implementations. Prototype transformation can be used to produce alternative parallel realisations: process placement on the target architecture may then be guided by prototype instrumentation. This approach is illustrated through the development of a parallel imperative implementation of a perspective inversion algorithm from a pure functional prototype.

articleTitle: Design Of Firing Scheme Using 8085 Microprocessor For Variable Frequency Three Phase Ac Power Controller
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A microprocessor based controller for a three phase ac power converter, operating on a variable frequency supply is discussed. This scheme is developed using 8085 microprocessor with minimum hardware. The firing angle of the power controller is maintained constant irrespective of the supply frequency. Any change in the firing angle is implemented within one sixth of a cycle, making the response of the system faster. The paper describes the complete hardware and software for the above.

articleTitle: On the relation between impulse response moments and locations of poles and zeros of a digital filter
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Conventional sensitivity measures in the study of quantization effects in digital filters involve cross terms of zeros and poles and are hard to express the effect of individual poles and zeros. We show a linear relation between the zeros and poles and the moments of the impulse response. We also show an interesting condition for the zeros of FIR low pass filter having linear phase and real coefficients.

articleTitle: Elimination Of Limit Cycles From A Fuzzy Petri Net For Drawing Stable Inferences In Expert Systems
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The paper presents a new technique for revision of fuzzy belief of a set of imprecise information embedded in fuzzy Petri net. Limit cycle behaviour, which is often exhibited during the belief revision process in the network, paralyses the mechanism of drawing inference in an expert system,embodying the fuzzy Petri net as the inference engine. The paper provides new algorithms for detection and elimination of limit cycles from a fuzzy Petri net. Instability in the reasoning process in expert systems can therefore be easily eliminated with the help of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: On Improving the Fault Detection and Reliability in FDDI Networks
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: FDDI (Fiber Distributed Data Interface) is a 100 Mbps token ring network with two counter rotating optical rings. Various possible faults (like lost token, link failures etc. ) are considered and fault detection and the ring recovery process in case of a failure and the reIiablfity mechanisms provided are studied. We suggest a new method to improve the fault detectim and ring recovery process. The performance improvement in terms of station queue length and the average delay is compared with the performance of the existing fault detection and ring recovery process through simulation. We also suggest a modification for the physical configuration of the FDDI networks within the guidelines set by the standard to make the network more reliable. It is shown that, unlike the existing FDDI network, full connectivity is maintained among the stations even when multiple single link failures occur. A distributed algorithm is proposed for link reconfiguration of the modified FDDI network when many successive as well as simultaneous link failures occur. The performance of the modified FDDI network under link failures is studied through simulation and compared with that of the existing FDDI network.

articleTitle: A General Purpose Communication Management System for Multi-User on Line and Real Time Systems to Telecom Management Centre
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Need for a suitable Communication Management System over a lower level Communication Protocol is often felt during the development of a large on line and real time application systems operating on data at distributed places and communicating over a private network. A Management Centre (or Head Office) interacting with its different activity centres (or Branch Offices) over a star network represents a typical environment of many such applications. General Purpose Communication Management System (GPCMS), presented in this paper, is an attempt towards combining and generalising the individual needs of such application systems. Having features of tunability to several applications, GPCMS has, as an illustration, been successfully adopted by a large multi-user on line and real time system of Telecom Management Centre which proved useful in formulating the ideas of GPCMS.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow Through Reduced Newton Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: First order gradient type of optimal power flow techniques have been extensively used until recently where their slow convergence rates when applied to large scale systems have been encountered. Second order Newton type methods have been proposed in recent time to improve the convergence characteristics. This paper presents an improved version of the Newton formulation that retains the fast convergence rates but reduces over-all computation time. With a brief description of the mathematical formulation the paper presents the results of studies carried out on a number of systems. The improvements in computation time are discussed on the basis of the comparative assessment.

articleTitle: S3L : a Fair Functional Language Implementing Infinite Sets
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: S3L/sup 1/ is a functional language, that allows easy manipulation of sets. Sets provide a better expressive power in many problems. Often, sets are modelled by lists, and predicates on sets are defined using implicit order over lists. In contrast, in S3L, sets are native objects. They can be finite or infinite, and for an efficient implementation multiple occurences of the same object are allowed. We describe, in the paper, the main features of the language, followed by a discussion on infinite sets. This leads us to deal with fairness, and tools expressing it, using a denotational approach.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Protocol for Real Time Computer Networks for Safety Applications
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A fail safe end-to-end protocol is one that delivers all packets ordered and without duplication [1,2]. Such a protocol for real time computer networks incorporating message priority levels is presented in this paper. The model, formal specifications and simulation results on a 8 node transputer network are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Analysis Of Series Resonant Converters
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The steady-state analysis of series resonant converters is presented using a frequency domain model. Generalized expressions for the resonant current and the capacitor voltage are derived. The possibility of multiple continuous conduction mode (MCM) when the power switches are supplied with continuous gate/base drive pulses is pointed out. Some important performance characteristics relating to output voltage, output current, switching frequency, feedback diode conduction angle are given. Some guide lines in the selection of component values and their ratings are given with an illustrative example. The model has been validated by comparing the results with those already published in the literature using a time-domain model.

articleTitle: A Methodology For Partial Verification And Validation Of OPS5-based Al Applications
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Verification and validation of AI systems is an important problem. In this article, we present a methodology for partial verification and validation of production system applications, in particular, OPS5-based applications. This methodology has two main parts in it. The first part, termed Domain-Independent Verification, involves finding certain properties and relations of productions by compile-time analysis. The second part, termed Systematic Testing, consists of generating the data-dependency graph, finding the set of distinct data-paths, and generating test data for each distinct data-path. We discuss how these two parts of the methodology contribute towards the partial verification and validation of OPS5-based applications.

publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper discusses design optimization of induction motor for irrigation pump application under realistic conditions, by taking input KVA as the objective function. Following the sensitivity analysis to effect suitable design modifications, it compares the optimized design with the standard design and highlights the performance of the motors based on such designs.

articleTitle: A hierarchical multiple access protocol for MAN's
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: A hierarchical multiple access protocol (HIMAP) is proposed for metropolitan area networks to achieve hign performance, suit multilevel architecture of networks, and support interconnection with LAN's. Several subsets of stations are assumed along the network trunk. A subset can be a branch or a local area network interconnected to it. Subsets access the trunk according to implicit token protocol. Stations access the channel with intra-subset protocol when the subset is polled, for which reservation CSMA/CD is considered as an example in this paper. HIMAP is completely distributed and less sensitive to network size. It is fair -for all stations, and yields bounded delay for real-time traffic. Finally, analysis and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: TRAMS - A Computer Network for Plant Environment
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: This paper describes the Computer Network installed at a Steel Plant in Central India for Traffic Management function. The movement of Railway Wagons and Locomotives used for loading and unloading of material in the Steel Plant is managed by an on-line computerised information system. The system comprises of one mini computer installed at a central site and 20 personal computers installed at remote sites. The data communication between the mini computer and remote PCS takes place through Radio links in a multiple access environment.

articleTitle: Natural Language Representatiom - A Connectionist Approach
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The work discusses a connectionist approach to the construction of syntactic and semantic represenations. The need to handle symbol processing and heuristic search to process natural language in real time, has prompted the, search for an alternative approach to tackle these issues. This has led to the cycle-intensive approach using a large number of very simple processors to get around the limitations of conventional symbolic processing. The system described in this work uses a sort and scan approach to assign lexical details to words. During the training phase of the syntactic module an incremental learning method to establish weak connections to represent the syntax of the connections to represent the syntax of the natural language by exposing the system to example syntactic constituent patterns and sentence patterns. A bottom-up parsing strategy is used to progressively fire word nodes, syntactic constituent nodes, using a marker propagation and constraint decision technique to maintain the relative ordering. The approacli creates a distributed representation of the parse tree and allows selective retrieval of parts of the structure. The semantic representation phase also works from the word nodes and utilizes projection rules to propagate markers and establish semantic connections after satisfying the semantic selectional restrictions imposed by the semantic descriptions. This marker propagation continues until a semantic structure has been associated with the sentence node.

articleTitle: Effect Of Chromatic Dispersion On The Performance Of A Coherent Ask Heterodyne Lightwave System
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: The effect of chromatic dispersion on the error performance of an optical heterodyne system with envelope detection has been reported. It is shown that the first order dispersion increases the probability of error.

abstract: An important consideration in the design of the communication network or a transportation network is the degree to which connectivity between given pairs of nodes is vulnerable to the failure or destruction of other links of the network.The introduction of redundancy in the network wiil increase its survivabtity, but at the same time increase the cost of construction. This leads to the problem of designing a minimum cost network to meet specific redundancy requirements.

articleTitle: Synchronization Strategies On The Points Of Turn-off Time Of Series-Connected Power Switching Elements
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: It is possible to produce a high voltage power converter by connecting the power semiconductor elements in series. However, simulations conduction at turn-on and simultaneous blocking at turn-off are unattainable because of the difference of their switching characteristics. Therefore, the series connection of semiconductor devices is very difficult in terms of control and protection. Generally for series connection, larger snubber capacitors are needed, which result in more losses and longer commutation times. This paper propose a novel algorithm which is able to implement not only the synchronization of the points of turn-on and turn-off time, but the dynamic voltage balancing in spite of the difference of switching characteristics. The proposed method is that the compensated control signals are attained from voltage feedback signals and applied to the series-connected power semiconductors independently. Computer simulation and experimental results verify its validity.

articleTitle: Consumer Load Control For Optimum Use Of Generating Capacity
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: Most power utilities have procedures for reducing the system load when their generation and outside purchases cannot meet the demand. In the present paper a scheme of automatic intelligent load shedding, by directly controlling consumer's loads is proposed. In the proposed scheme the demand limiters are installed at each of the medium and large power consumer end which are centrally controlled by the computer installed at the substation. The demand limiters shed load in steps, adjustable as per consumers convenience. The demand limiters to achieve the direct load control, introducing artificial intelligence, based on proposed scheme, is designed and tested in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Performance measurement of operations administration & maintenance activities of the SESS switch
publicationTitle: TENCON '91. Region 10 International Conference on EC3-Energy, Computer, Communication and Control Systems
abstract: In the design of compleml systems, the performance of the system is often a very important design parameter. Performance requirements are defined in the early stages of the development cycle, and various steps can be taken in each development stage to ensure that the requirements are met. Systematic performance measurement is a key technique used by the SESS(V Telephone Switch project in the integration/system test stages to ensure control and to performance requirements. In fact, at certain stages of the development life-cycle, and for certain kinds of performance problems, systematic measurement is the only effective detection technique. for the past several years, the authors have been involved in improving process and techniques of measuring performance for Operations, Administration & Maintenance (OA&M) activities in the SESS Switch. This paper describes the, experience gained from this effort. Section 2 provides a brief overview of the SESS architecture, its development cycles, a model which is used for dealing with performance issues/problems in the and The challenges and problems in measuring performance OA&M activities. Section 3 describes the process and are used in QA&M performance measurements: approach and planning and scheduling; workloads and measurement control, and finally the measuring and analysis techniques. Section 4 discusses some of the experiences and Section 5 lists areas for future improvements.
